partners.name: Bender Defenders
partners.description:
Come and train in a queer and trans space far away from "mainstream gym culture". Professional Muay Thai fighter and trans athlete Luca makes sure that these classes are taught in a lighthearted and fun way. 

Beginners and first timers welcome.

What to expect:

Participants are not asked to fight or hit each other: you will be provided with pads to hit and gloves to do all the hitting with! This is a playful environment where queer and trans people come to train, make friends, have fun and explore their own strength through Muay Thai and partner work.
You do not have to be good at it or know how to do it from the beginning. 

Everything you will learn in this classes can be used in self defence, however we do not run these classes with the aim of "having to defend ourself" in mind. As a community we are already very hypervigilant and we do not need reminders that we might be in danger. We have created this space for queer and trans people to play through the medium of sport.
partners.summary: BENDER DEFENDERS is a community empowerment, Muay Thai and self-defence training movement.

partners.name: Clémentine Bedos
partners.description:
Facilitated by transdisciplinary artist Clémentine Bedos as part of their Phd research and Generation Delta* residency at Goldsmiths CCA. 

Clémentine Bedos is a London-based artist, researcher, and educator with a background in law, philosophy, and fine arts. Their socially engaged practice explores the interrelated phenomena of identity, mind/body and consciousness within the terms of our present hegemonic modes of identity. Clémentine was guided to the nondual philosophy of Śaiva Tantra by her grandmother and has been working with its teachings to heal transgenerational trauma and empower subaltern groups since 2019.

*Generation Delta is a 4-year project (2022-2026) led by 6 members of the Black Female Professors Forum designed to lay the foundations for a long-term increase in the number of BAME female professors in higher education institutions in England.
partners.summary: Clémentine Bedos is a London-based artist, researcher, and educator with a background in law, philosophy, and fine arts.

partners.name: Dalston Superstore
partners.description:
Dalston Superstore is East London's premiere queer pleasure palace. Functioning in equal parts as a thriving queer club, cabaret spot, cafe, gallery and community space, the venue proudly caters to London's diverse LGBTQ+ community. 

Dalston Superstore us as much a thriving music-centred club as it is a front-running drag and performance space. We've played host to dance music heavy-hitters such as Honey Dijon, The Blessed Madonna and the late Andrew Weatherall, and hosted residencies at Glastonbury's Block 9, Lovebox and Winterville. Our weekend Drag Brunch has gained cult-status, with many a bleary-eyed queer rolling through the doors for a hangover cure, having left Club Tantrum or Femmme Fraiche hours before. 

Supporting and uplifting LGBTQ+ charities and organisations is also central to who we are, and we are proud to regularly support Positive East, The Outside Project, Albert Kennedy Trust and more. We continue to change and develop as a queer space - if you'd like to contribute to our every-growing web of collaborators please get in touch!
partners.summary: Dalston Superstore is East London's premiere queer pleasure palace. Functioning in equal parts as a thriving queer club, cabaret spot, cafe, gallery and community space.

partners.name: LGBT Hero
partners.description:
LGBT HERO aims to improve the health, enhance the wellbeing and champion the rights of LGBTQ+ people. LGBT HERO provides LGBTQ+ people with accurate and credible information so they can build skills that enable them to make informed choices about their health and wellbeing. We encourage LGBTQ+ people to create social change in our communities by providing a platform where they are heard and valued. 

LGBT HERO wants to see a world where LGBTQ+ people have the same opportunities in life as all other people, and are not disadvantaged by health or social inequalities because of their sexuality or identity.

LGBT HERO is also the organisation behind GMFA - the sexual wellbeing project for gay, bi and trans men who have sex with men providing frank and honest info, advice, support and campaigns about all things sex and sexual health while providing support to men living with HIV.

partners.name: Likewise
partners.description:
Likewise is a charity and community centre in Swiss Cottage, Camden, with a history rooted in supporting the wellbeing of marginalised and isolated people and communities. We work with people from diverse backgrounds and circumstances, meeting them where they are in their lives to support their sense of wellbeing, belonging, and community. Our vision is a society where everyone can thrive and feel safe to be themselves through supportive relationships, genuine connections, and inclusive environments.

We deliver support through community activities at our hub, as well as one to-one support in the community. Our support is led by the people we work with, recognising that we’re all equally human. We do things with people rather than to or for them. The energy and input of our vibrant community is essential to our offer.

We also aim to influence change within the broader health and care system by bringing our values and ways of working to different partnerships including Camden Council and the NHS. We want to see organisations and services become more human, adaptable, and responsive to people’s circumstances.

We have been delivering person-centred support for more than 30 years. Putting relationships first, we’re alongside people helping them find their place and navigate life.
partners.summary: Likewise is a charity and community centre in Swiss Cottage, Camden, with a history rooted in supporting the wellbeing of marginalised and isolated people and communities.

partners.description:
Established in 1972 London Friend is the UK’s oldest Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual and Trans charity. We are here to support the health and mental wellbeing of the LGBT community in and around London.

We offer counselling and support around issues such as same-sex relationships, sexual and gender identity and promoting personal growth and self-confidence. We're also home to Antidote - the UK's oldest LGBT drug and alcohol service. Our social groups provide a safe space to meet and socialise as an alternative to the bar and club scene.

partners.name: London LGBTQ+ Community Centre
partners.description:
It will serve as a meeting place,  a place to build connections, to reduce isolation through intergenerational contact, to provide information through a  signposting and information service and a place where services for the LGBTQ+  community are facilitated under one roof. Similar centres have transformed the wellbeing and connectedness of the community in their area, and that’s what we will do too.

The London LGBTQ+ Community Centre will be a safe space for the community to relax, meet up and hang out, as well as to receive the services existing groups and charities provide. Our Cafe will provide a sober hangout spot for anyone of any age or identity to come along to. In order to be accessible and combat poverty and classism, our cafe will follow the same model as the Sidney Street Cafe in Manchester, and will be genuinely affordable. We will have multipurpose rooms for a variety of events and purposes that fit within our charitable aims of promoting social inclusion and championing equality and diversity.

We will provide a home for the community to relax, be themselves and feel safe, working with existing groups and charities to facilitate and deliver services to combat isolation, improve wellbeing and connection to the community. A place where people can meet and make strong connections, where chosen families are built and flourish and where intergenerational socialisation is at the heart of it all – where everyone, of all ages and backgrounds, is welcome.
partners.summary: Inspired by other major cities’ LGBTQ+ centres, our goal is to set up a safe, sober, intergenerational community centre and cafe for the LGBTQ+ community of London.

partners.name: PECS Education
partners.description:
Our names are Kole Fulmine and Georgie Okell, we are trans masc, non-binary personal trainers and fitness professionals.

What will we do in this hour long session? We will lift weights and use bodyweight movements in order to condition and tone areas of the body that you may be experiencing dysphoria with. This is an open and safe forum to discuss our trans bodies and will be ever evolving in terms of the way we train. We will guide you through correct alignment and positioning of weights so that you can make some serious gains and avoid injury. If you're looking for somewhere to talk through hormone use and the impact of taking T on your body, or even somewhere to share lived experience of being trans, then this is it. 

We would love to hold space for all those who identify on the queer spectrum, and would prefer to avoid labels, however, from personal (quite detrimental) experience the fitness industry just does not work in that way. (Another discussion topic!) So, this space is intentionally enclosed as we feel the industry lacks a class entirely devoted to us trans bois.

You don't need to bring anything other than some water, or a container to fill up. Please message us directly if you would like advice on clothing, or any other concerns you have regarding the gym itself. Basis Gym will be closed to other members during our session. There are toilets and changing rooms available. Please be aware these are labelled in a binary way and public.
partners.summary: PECS EDUCATION - is a trans masc, non-binary strength and conditioning class.

partners.name: Pxssy Palace
partners.description:
WHAT IS PXSSY PALACE?
Pxssy Palace is an arts platform rooted in intentional nightlife, celebrating Black, Indigenous and People of Colour who are Queer, Intersex, Trans or Non-binary. We provide space to dance, connect and engage, whilst encouraging consent, sexual freedom, pleasure, expression and exploration of our authentic selves.

WHO CAN COME TO PXSSY PALACE?
Honestly, anyone. This has always been the case, BUT we do ask those who are not from the community that we are celebrating (Queer Women, Intersex, Non-binary and Trans BIPOC) to ask themselves why they are coming? Who are they coming with? And if they are coming, how are they contributing to the space? 

WHY?
Ways that allies and accomplices can contribute to Pxssy Palace and our community include:

- Paying more money for entry
- Giving generously to the taxi fund
- Supporting your family and friends who are from the community, both in and outside of our events
- Being aware of the space you take up, how your behaviour may make others feel and to not walk the runway

INTENTIONAL SPACES
Pxssy Palace has a zero tolerance policy for sexual and/or physical harassment or violence. Anyone who does not follow this policy while partying with us will be asked to leave. If you experience behaviour in any form then please report it to PP Support. 

PP SUPPORT
PP Support are a group of 5-15 trained QTIBPOC who look after the space and our guests. Their role is to bridge the gap between party goers and the security/venue team, and to look out for your wellbeing. The team is identifiable by pink led light arm bands. PP Support will be on hand throughout the venue if you need to report a problem and if you cannot find one there will also be a designated PP support area. This area will be located on the venue map that is posted before the club night to find out where they will be stationed. PP Support are trained by Pxssy Palace and by Good Night Out who provide training on how to better understand, respond to and prevent sexual harassment and assault. 

THE RUNWAY
The Runway is an attitude and confidence based competition and is a space for those who want to be celebrated by the whole club at once. We encourage those who are not dancers, or dressed to the theme to also take part. Please check social media for set times to find out what time the runway starts. 

THE THEME
Each of our events have a theme - however there is never any pressure to dress up. Come in whatever makes you feel comfortable. 

FOOD
We aim to provide food vendors with meat and vegan options at every event that we do. Please check our social media prior to an event of ours to find out what will be on offer

THE SANCTUARY
We always ensure that there is space for us to dance, but for those that want to chill, 'The Sanctuary is a place to sit and relax, rehydrate, and take a moment away from the dance floor. 'The Sanctuary' differs for each of our events and features multiple vendors for you to enjoy such as massage, beauty therapy, hair care, art, and a community library. Check the Instagram to find out which vendors are there.

THE TAXI FUND
Our Taxi Fund is set up to contribute to BIPOC trans & disabled guests’ travel expenses to get home safely from our events. We collect donations for the Taxi Fund on the door, throughout the night and on our PayPal which is linked on our Instagram and website. Please email in advance or let us know on your way in if you require this service. Please be aware that taxi requests close 30 minutes before the event is over and the maximum amount we can book is £30. Please pre book before an event by adding your name, postcode and event you require a taxi home from here/link in bio

MUSIC
The music will vary throughout the night from Club, Bashment, House, Grime, Ballroom, Jersey, R&G, Techno, Bollywood, Garage, Gqom, Amapiano, UK Funky, Dembow, Bass, Footwork and much, much more. 

One room will always feature DJs who play R&B, Hip-Hop, Afrobeats and Pop every month although this will sometimes be heard in the mainroom too. 

We book DJ’s who make noise, tell stories, teach us something new and hold our emotions of joy, rage and sadness. 

We encourage you to check them out before the show and support them on and off the dancefloor.

BUDDY SYSTEM
The first hour of our events is a dedicated slot for solo ravers to meet and make new friends before the party gets busy. There will be Pxssy Palace staff to welcome you and introduce you to make friends.
partners.summary: Pxssy Palace is an arts platform rooted in intentional nightlife, celebrating Black, Indigenous and People of Colour who are Queer, Intersex, Trans or Non-binary.

We are a friendly crew, we try to socialise as well after the run. Sessions are normally one hour long, they vary each week. It will be a mixture of a long run (up to 8km), hill sprints, paced runs, and sprints or running games. We don't have a specific pace that you need to run at, ALL levels are welcome. Your sessions will be run by Kole, a trans-masc running coach. I'm a UKA England Athletics certified coach and running leader. Or Sam, who is a UKA England Athletics certified Leader in Running Fitness.

The project is aimed at transgender and gender diverse people, with any gender history, at any stage of their journey, their families and carers, who are looking to find other members of their community.

The T&Coffee Trans Network was founded in 2019 by a transgender woman who identified the limitations of online only platforms. We aim to bridge that gap, through allowing members of a marginalised and largely online community, to have a safe and friendly space to turn to.

Whilst everyone was impacted by the global Covid-19 Pandemic, the network was able to continue providing a welcoming environment to a global community through specific online resources. Now our face-to-face events are restarting as it becomes safe to gather as groups. 

The T&Coffee Trans Network is a not about profit, with no joining, attendance or membership fees for anyone who wants to find support.

TransLondon is a discussion/support group for all members of the ‘trans’ community, whatever their gender identity (or identities) and whatever stage in their ‘transition’ they have reached (if at all). However, all members must themselves be trans-identified or ‘questioning’.

The Aims of TransLondon are to:

- provide a safe place to explore and express your personal gender identity
- combat isolation
- provide support with information and resources
- provide a space where all trans people can socialize, share experiences and exchange ideas
- combat transphobia
- promote greater acceptance and rights for all transpeople
- provide help & advice for transpeople who want to support their friends, family & colleagues
- provide advice and support with transitioning
- above all, the group is intended to foster a sense of inclusion and celebration of each of us as unique and valued (trans) people.

With donations from the local community The TIN Wardrobe aims to help people access clothing for free so they can be who they want to be.

partners.name: Trans in the City
partners.description:
Trans in the City aims to pool the expertise, role models and dynamism of partner organisations, sharing this knowledge freely with any organisation that needs it.

It is free to join and is open to any group whether public or private, large or small. All services are provided free of charge.

Trans in the City understands that businesses, and society, are on a journey and that no one is perfect; there is always room for improvement. Engaging with Trans in the City will provide a safe space to discuss where you could improve your practices and policies, offering a judgement free environment to help start your journey in trans awareness. 
​
Through our collaboration we can make the world a better and more inclusive place together. If you’d like more information or would like to join please feel free to contact us.
partners.summary: Trans in the City​ is an open collaboration between global organisations, corporates and companies to further inclusion of transgender, non-binary and gender diversity in business by raising awareness

partners.name: Trans Media Watch
partners.description: Trans Media Watch is run by volunteers and depends on ordinary people within the trans community to be its eyes and ears. It aims to reflect the concerns of those people and of the community as a whole. Trans Media Watch is concerned with issues affecting all people covered by the transgender umbrella. It deals with cases involving transsexual people, genderqueer and androgyne people, crossdressers, and intersex people. As well as tackling problems after the fact, Trans Media Watch aims to build up links with media organisations and watchdog bodies to help them work towards improved service in the future. It can provide advice to journalists and programme makers who are unsure how to approach sensitive issues, and undertakes research to provide information useful to public bodies working in this field.
partners.summary: Trans Media Watch is an organisation that aims to combat prejudiced, sensationalist and inaccurate depictions of trans people in the media.

partners.name: Trans Radio UK (TRUK)
partners.description:
Trans Radio UK is the only trans radio station in the UK and probably the world. We are proud to support the whole of the trans community as well as the LGBT spectrum including allies, with the vast majority of our presenters being trans or non-binary and located in UK or around the world. We are a community radio station for the community and are not profit making.

We are currently listened to in nearly 100 countries and are live 24/7 with a vast range of different shows, music styles and undertake community focused topical interviews. We pride ourselves on being a platform for members of all the community to showcase their talents, whether they are a presenter, DJ or musician and freely promote charitable community events.

We connect all different people within the community and reach out to those that are unable to leave their homes so they still feel part of a community. We are a community radio station for the community run by the community.

partners.name: VFDalston
partners.description:
Femmifesto

VFD has always been a safe space for all, in the light of neoconservatism and the need for intersectional unity we want to reiterate the beliefs and practice that we stand by. 

…………………………………………………………………………………

VFD is a space to imagine, create and take action. 

It is place to make transgressive imagery, a home to the outlaw rebel visionary and a space to discuss the critical alteration of the oppressive status quo.

We ask in the interests of liberation and for the enjoyment of all who find their way to vFd that you
 observe the following:

 

Respect yourself and everyone else. 

 

Glorify all bodies for their individual beauty and power. 

 

Celebrate each person’s self-determined gender. 

 

Always establish positive consent … it’s hot! 

 

Remember to frequently tell your friends you love them. 

 

If at any point during your time at VFD you feel our code of conduct is not being observed then please tell one of the vFd staff so that they may rectify the problem immediately. 

We understand that each of us is on a journey of constant transformation and that as a community we are here to love each other through the challenges of dismantling the oppressive imperialist white supremacist capitalist heteronormative patriarchy in order to live equally in shared freedom. 

Lastly, we ask you to be patient with us at VFD. Change is the only constant in life. We will always take on new knowledge and strive to better serve the community.
partners.summary: An originator and incubator of queer arts and entertainment in Dalston, VFD has hosted, promoted and nurtured emerging and superstar LGBTQI performers, acts and nights.

events.name: November\'s Friendly Transgender Social Meetup London
events.description:
\*\*Are you Trans and want to meet other trans people in a safe and
social environment?\*\*

Join me and your fellow trans lovelies for a relaxed meetup on
\*\*Thursday November 16th at 19.30 in the Soho, central London
area.\*\*

This place has a great buzz and we have our own private space booked!
It\'s a sneaky way to start the weekend early. Come and join us :)

\*\*RSVP NOW\*\*

We have a private area upstairs in the venue, which is plenty of space
for us all to chat, hear each other and relax.

Thursday is the new start of the weekend. Let\'s use this opportunity to
make some new friends and chat about whatever pleases you.

This event will suit you if you are new to attending the meetup or are
one of our wonderful regulars. It is a popular evening with lots of
different people popping in. There is no need to be nervous. We are all
very friendly and welcoming. You\'ll feel right at home. :)

\*\*What is this meetup?\*\*

This is a relaxed, friendly and inclusive meetup for the trans people of
London. This is an opportunity to make new friends and chat over a
sneaky Thursday drink.

\*\*Who is it for?\*\*

Everyone from the trans community is welcome. This is an opportunity to
be yourself, whatever you identify as. We are inclusive and happy to
welcome you.

\*\*How does it work?\*\*

Your host Ray has booked a private area in a pub in the Soho area. All
you have to do is RSVP and then Ray will message you on the day with the
event location. Then, all you have to do is show up.

Ray will make sure that you meet some new people and get a chance to get
to know your fellow trans buddies. He is very friendly and will welcome
you and make sure you feel comfortable and happy.

It is free to attend, just buy yourself a drink at the bar.

\*\*Please Note:\*\* RSVP is a must as the location (based around Soho)
will be sent by email on the day to those who have RSVP\'d only. RSVP
closes at 16.00 on the day of the event.

\*\*RSVP NOW\*\*
events.summary: November\'s Friendly Transgender Social Meetup London

Gather your friends, put on your fiercest outfits, and prepare for a

events.name: Queer House Party
events.description:
THAT’S RIGHT. WE’RE BACK. Tickets for our first event of 2023 are on
sale now. We’ve had such an incredible time taking QHP on the road, but
we’ve been missing what we love most - creating our own spaces to share
with our community. Bringing together radical and liberatory politics
with some of the best performances, music, and art from the DIY queer
scene. NEW VENUE: We’ve found our new home at Studio 9294, Hackney Wick.
It’s a huge warehouse space with multiple rooms - meaning we will have a
stacked lineup across two rooms with spaces to watch shows, dance, and
chill. TRANS PPL TO THE FRONT: Queer House Party is run by a
predominantly trans team - and while we are a queer party, moving
forward, we’re going to be centering the ongoing fight for trans
liberation and the trans community at all of our parties. Queer House
Party is for everyone - but trans people to the front. EVERYONE IN:
We’ve done our best to keep ticket prices down for everyone. Tickets are
on a sliding scale from £7.50-17.50. If this is still a barrier for you,
please drop us a message, and we will add you to our free list. IMPROVED
ONLINE PARTY: In true alignment with our roots as a party that started
online, we still run our events with live-streams so that anyone can be
included in the club, regardless of geography, financial situation,
disability, and other needs. To make this happen, we’re working with a
brand new streaming service, CastRooms. We’re talking multiple cameras
with high-quality video and audio for everyone who wants to join us
virtually. SAME ACCESS: Studio 9294 is a wheelchair-accessible venue.
Both our IRL and URL events will have BSL, AD, and CC available during
the shows. Free tickets are available for carers and PAs. We will be
following this post up with a more detailed breakdown of the space, but
if you have any specific questions, drop us a line at
queerhouseparty@gmail.com.COVID POLICY: We ask that everyone tests
before attending to try and keep the party as safe as possible. If you
can’t get hold of a test before the event, there will be a covid testing
station outside the venue. We will not ask for proof that you have
tested. Cover image - Bex Wade

events.name: Pumping Velvet - til 4am!
events.description:
The nights are growing longer, our limbs are getting colder and the rain
pours down. Come and shake off your seasonal depression and warm those
feet with a night of ecstatic dancing at Pumping Velvet! Leading our
winter warmer is Puerto Rican-American DJ and producer Juan Ramos. Juan
is a resident at Berlin’s fabled Cocktail d’Amore party and his elusive
mixing and fearless selection works to keep the floor guessing but
always dancing. Joining Juan downstairs will be Michael Upson, founder
and resident DJ of Leeds based, pumping queer club night, Love Muscle.
Love Muscle is rightly regarded as one of the best underground queer
parties in the country and Michael will be bringing some of that magic
down with him as he plays Superstore for the very first time. Opening
proceedings will be babyschön, who hosts a regular show on NARR radio
and plays just the kind of lithe and sleazy italo, boogie & synth-pop we
love so much. Upstairs sees a wavy night of music as Edith Escobar and
Sports Maximum step up with sets bound to span amapiano, R&B and club
edits, before rising star Goh Well closes out the night with a cute and
fun blend of house and garage. Come pump some velvet ? £7 BEFORE 11 /
£10 AFTER

events.name: Folktales Presents Afro Groove & Latin Rhythm Party
events.description:
Join us for our second segment of Folktales World Music live at the
Folklore where we are joined this time round by the legendary Bene Tally
Band of Senegalese and West African heritage and the rhythm centric
Andean Afro-latin fusion delights of LOKANDES.

Converging at the magnificent forest of lore on 186 Hackney Road - Bene
Tally Band which was formerly initiated by master Dembis Thioung, brings
with them a unique and organic sound of Senegalese/ West African
percussion rhythms, ancestral songs and choreographies which weave
various Afro-Latin traditional musical forms and instruments against the
bass heavy sound of the West African Dundun drum.

Expect to be entranced by the engaging and co-creative atmosphere of
traditional song, reflexive dance at the primal rhythm and the
opportunity to connect to your deeper self, others and life itself
through the deeply hypnotic and seductive rhythm.

We’ll then be graced by the unconventional and alternative sound of
Lokandes - a name reflecting the eclectic fusion of Andean instruments
with contemporary genres such as Reggae, Cumbia, Ska, Jazz, Rumba Folk
and funky Latin rhythms all of which make this band an experience not to
be missed.

The band brings together a diverse cast of musicians from Peru, Bolivia,
Panama, Chile, Spain & Cuba and is lead by their charismatic leader
Kanti of Peruvian descent horning their unique sound, alongside socially
conscious lyrics and a super-tight rhythm section drawing awareness to
the diverse Latin-American and global cultures.

In true collaborative Folktales fashion, we will end the night with a
collective improv jam with both bands joined and supported by the
musical gifts of Gnawa Master - Simo Lagnawi and the Audio.sync
Collective for an unforgettable night of dancing, connecting and
celebration of culture and unity in rhythm.

Secure your ticket and see you Friday 24th at the Folklore, 186 Hackney
Rd. E2 7QL.

events.name: Frank Malachi - Quantum Happiness
events.description:
**About**

Frank Malachi presents their EP Quantum Happiness, a reflection on
sentience, artificiality and virtual immersiveness. The album is a
journey through the arpeggiated wave-forms of the Omnichord recapturing
much of the 80\'s nostalgia. Pedalled by the era of Casio keyboards and
machine drum effects, Quantum Happiness is shaped like a scientific love
letter - (“Oxytocin+Serotonin+Dopamine”).

**Stage Times**

20:00 Bella Unwin

21:00 Frank Malachi

**Bio**

Frank Malachi @frank\_malachi\_music

Frank Malachi is an Audio-Visual Artist, Producer and
Multi-Instrumentalist. Their EP entitled “Quantum Happiness” is a
philosophical axe that excavates the layers of our growingly
desensitized bodies, speaking volumes through choruses of electronic
voices in a mating dance, in turn confronting our computerised selves.
In a progressively dehumanised culture where virtual immersiveness and
artificiality take precedence an atomic autopsy of happiness looks at
the economy of emotional value through much of this digital age.

Frank examines the flux of happiness through a wider lens, influencing
the thermostat arrow movements between the latitudes of lust or sorrow.
Franks music casts a graphic of extreme polar ends making pure
contemplation not so far from absolute alienation.

Will Pinocchio ever be a real boy? Will the cyborg ever destroy?

Bella Unwin @bellaunwin

Bella Unwin is a London based producer baking up beeps, boops and funky
loops. After experimenting with varying different genres of electronic
dance music, Bella’s sets explore 80’s beats and aesthetics, from techno
to house music. Dancing is also expected - but not compulsory.

events.description:
\*\*It\'s been a big year! Let\'s all celebrate together and enjoy a few
drinks and some fun!\*\*

Join me and your fellow trans lovelies for a relaxed meetup on
\*\*Thursday Dec 14th at 19.30 in the Soho, central London area.\*\*

\*\*As its Christmas, lets do a Cheesy Christmas thing and wear
something Christmassy! 😃\*\*

This place has a great buzz and we have our own private space booked!
It\'s a sneaky way to start the weekend early. Come and join us :)

\*\*RSVP NOW\*\*

We have a private area upstairs in the venue, which is plenty of space
for us all to chat, hear each other and relax.

Thursday is the new start of the weekend. Let\'s use this opportunity to
make some new friends and chat about whatever pleases you.

This event will suit you if you are new to attending the meetup or are
one of our wonderful regulars. It is a popular evening with lots of
different people popping in. There is no need to be nervous. We are all
very friendly and welcoming. You\'ll feel right at home. :)

\*\*What is this meetup?\*\*

This is a relaxed, friendly and inclusive meetup for the trans people of
London. This is an opportunity to make new friends and chat over a
sneaky Thursday drink.

\*\*Who is it for?\*\*

Everyone from the trans community is welcome. This is an opportunity to
be yourself, whatever you identify as. We are inclusive and happy to
welcome you.

\*\*How does it work?\*\*

Your host Ray has booked a private area in a pub in the Soho area. All
you have to do is RSVP and then Ray will message you on the day with the
event location. Then, all you have to do is show up.

Ray will make sure that you meet some new people and get a chance to get
to know your fellow trans buddies. He is very friendly and will welcome
you and make sure you feel comfortable and happy.

It is free to attend, just buy yourself a drink at the bar.

\*\*Please Note:\*\* RSVP is a must as the location (based around Soho)
will be sent by email on the day to those who have RSVP\'d only. RSVP
closes at 16.00 on the day of the event.

\*\*RSVP NOW\*\*

events.description:
\*\*Join Us For Our Brand New Book Club.\*\*

\*\*Thursday January 18th 2024\*\*  
\*\*19.30 – 21.00, London UK (GMT)\*\*  
\*\*Kennington Area & Zoom\*\*

\*\*Available in-person and online. While we have booked a location, we
will also have the ability for your to join via zoom.\*\*

\*\*We are thrilled to announce this new meetup activity that will
happen quarterly.\*\*

As one of the requests from members we are delighted to make this event
a reality. Participating is very easy. All you have to do is read the
book below and then come to the meetup with your book and anything
you\'d like to discuss about the book. Nothing is off the table!

The book club will be supported by your host and will ensure that
everyone both in-person and online get an opportunity to discuss their
thoughts on the book.

\*\*The book we are going to discuss is:\*\*  
Amateur, A Reckoning with Gender, Identity, and Masculinity.

\*\*\[You can buy your copy via Amazon
HERE\]([https://www.amazon.co.uk/Amateur-True-Story-About-Makes-ebook/dp/B079HW5N56/ref=sr\_1\_1?crid=J9HY65I994C2&amp;keywords=amateur+a+reckoning&amp;qid=1700232914&amp;sprefix=amateur+a+reckoning%2Caps%2C80&amp;sr=8-1][1])\*\*

We \*\*DO NOT\*\* get any money for the book purchased. That\'s between
you and the author.

\*\*Who this is for:\*\*  
Anyone who is transgender or supporting transgender and wants to do
something a little different. To enjoy themselves and take some down
time while expressing themselves through art. This is a friendly and
supportive environment where everyone, regardless of their artistic
abilities are welcome.

\*\*WHEN YOU RSVP Please message Ray to let us know if you will attend
in person or via Zoom.\*\*

\*\*About Us:\*\*  
This event is part of a series of events run by the London Transgender
Meetup Group, sponsored by Lambeth Council and supported by LGBT Hero.

\### Sign Up Now To Secure Your Place

\*\*We will have to limit numbers to make sure that we can host the
event properly, so please RSVP now to avoid disappointment.\*\*

events.name: DOGZ OR GODZ
events.description:
Dogz or Godz possess the audacity of hip-hop and the rebellious spirit
of punk.

The London-based band kicks mediocrity firmly in the b\*llox. Their
first single, \'SCUM\', was released in March 2023. Legend has it that
Liam Howlett of ‘The Prodigy’ heard the original demo and liked it so
much that he asked if he could sprinkle a little dirt on it. The result
was a sonic bullet to the brain, swiftly followed by the anthems
\'ENERGY,\' \'F\*\*K IT,\' and \'HARD,\' each hitting the top of the
charts on iTunes and Amazon. July 2023, they completely sold out their
first ever gig while headlining the Camden Rocks Festival.

The Camden gig skyrocketed Dogz or Godz\'s profile, catching the
attention of one of Europe\'s largest festivals, Boomtown, and its
70,000-strong audience. Outside of London, the band is relatively
unknown, that is about to change. Boomtown invited Dogz or Godz to close
out their Vault Stage on August 13, 2023. The crowd couldn\'t get enough
of their festival anthems and charismatic stage presence, leading to a
flood of demands for their next gig. In October 2023, Dogz or Godz
performed for Darco Recordings, a new label led by former Island Records
CEO Darcus Beese. Dogz or Godz are more than just a band; it\'s a
rebellion in motion. Their music resonates with outcasts, rebels,
nonconformists, and those who refuse to bow to the masses. With their
middle finger firmly up, the D.O.G. continue to stick it to the man. DIG
THE NEW BREED...

events.name: Pumping Velvet

stuffing are always to be found at a Pumping Velvet party. For their
January do PV are teaming up with Manchester-based All Hands on Deck, a
collective for women, trans and non-binary DJs. Not just a famed Tinashe
bop, AHOD work to broaden participation in the underground-dance music
scene through their open-deck parties and DJ workshops, which they have
run at festivals like We Out Here, Supernormal and Headroom.  AHOD deck
residents Abena, ANNa & Hayter Player are also incredible DJs, each with
their own distinctive style, blending a wide-range of boops, bangers,
bleeps and bops. Together they will be taking over our beloved sweatbox
basement all night long. Check out Abena’s recent Boiler Room for
receipts on the damage they do in the club! Upstairs local Dalston hero
and TRANSENDANCE DJ Mads Mads, Balamii radio resident Bratmode and
Frizzy D, founder of the queer events collective Hunnisuckle, will take
us through to the early hours with a diverse mix of pop, R&BA, garage
and global bangers.  Come pump some velvet! £7 BEFORE 11 / £10 AFTER

events.name: Charlie Barnes + Hannah Lou Clark + Foxette Moxy
events.description:
Charlie Barnes announces his first London headline show since before the
you-know-what, at the beautiful FOLKLORE.

Hailing from the midlands, Charlie is a musician who wears many varied
hats. Since 2010, he has released five albums (four under his own name,
one as the lead singer and songwriter of alt-country duo The Society
Pages) and was the arranger and musical director behind Bastille’s MTV
Unplugged live album. As well as making music of his own, Charlie has
spent the last eight and a half years as Bastille’s touring member,
playing guitar, keys, bass, percussion and backing vocals, performing
all over the world on some of its most celebrated stages. He was also
the opening act for the band’s 2018 ‘ReOrchestrated’ tour, performing
acoustic renditions of songs from his ‘Oceanography’ album, and was at
the production and mixing helm for two songs from the band’s most recent
studio album release, ‘Give Me The Future & Dreams of the Past’.

Support on the night will come from Charlie\'s good friend Adam Smith,
known for his work with the band Temples, who will be making his first
live appearance as \'Foxette Moxy\', a new psychedelic pop solo project.
Also performing will be one of Charlie\'s favourite artists, the amazing
Hannah Lou Clark, who plays grungy, lo-fi pop with wickedly smart
melodies.

events.name: Queer Family Day with Drag Tales
events.description:
Bookings
at: [https://www.outsavvy.com/event/18181/queer-family-day-with-drag-tales][1]

Join us at The Common Press Bookshop on **11th February** from 12 pm to
4 pm and** 16th February** from 11 am -12 pm for a Queer Family Day with
Drag Tales during the half-term break. Relax and enjoy the day with
stories by one of our fabulous drag artists. ** Free children\'s tickets
and Pay What You Can tickets for adults are available.**

 

**About Drag Tales**

Books like Where The Wild Things Are, Penguin, Girls, The Hug, and many
other classic stories will be read. The focus is to have children see
books they know and love being read by gender-diverse fabulous beings
that exist all across our society. By using stories they’re familiar
with, the whole environment becomes familiar and comfortable.

Expect the unexpected, there might be some singing and if the kids are
old enough,  there might also be some games. Kids (as well as the
parents, guardians, or carers) will have time to ask questions at the
end to help further understand drag queens, gender fluidity, and why we
are wearing whatever it is we are wearing!

* Children must be accompanied by a guardian
* Children\'s details should not be included when buying tickets
* There is a baby-changing toilet and accessible toilets 

NOTE: Please keep in mind that space is limited, so make sure to secure
your spot early. If you plan to bring a buggy with you, there will be
space to store them.



[1]: https://www.outsavvy.com/event/18181/queer-family-day-with-drag-tales

events.name: RIPOSTE - THE QUEER ART RAVE
events.description:
Riposte is a queer art-rave aiming to facilitate connections between
strangers. A full on sweaty RAVE where you have nice spaces for good
chats, installations, performances, everything to make good memories and
have fun. This is a large scale event on 4 floors, 8 rooms (2
dancefloors, 1 playroom, 1 chill room, 1 performance room, 2 bars). It
is mainly attended by alternative queer people across the whole LGBT+
spectrum with many gender non-confirming people. Strong allies are
welcome 🏳️‍🌈🏳️‍⚧️ This is a RAVE, be ready to SWEAT. We will open at 9pm
with a "social" , a moment before the music start to meet new people and
make cute connections and at 5.30am until 6am in the Courtyard: free
BREAKFAST so you have time to gather your thoughts and find your
friends.Ceasefire now
🇵🇸❤️----------------------------------ACCESSIBILITY INFORMATIONS-Stairs
across the venue (both of the main dance floors are up long flights of
stairs, roughly 30 each). -Groundfloor (chill space, playroom, bar
&amp; quieter room) accessible with no stairs, levelled access,
accessible toilets (please ask: there is 4 different toilets ground
floor so it can be tricky to find. ). Please note that the courtyard
floor partially has cobbles.-Some areas are quite dark (stairs).-Strobe
lights -If you do not have the means to pay for a ticket, please send us
a DM on instagram or email us at least a few days before the event. We
encourage to pay at least concession price as it is a hella pricey
&amp; time consuming event to put on, put we can also offer free
tickets if needed. This offers if only available before we are sold
out.-Covid: we follow the U.K. gov guidelines and tests are not required
upon entry but welfare has self test kids as well as masks upon
demands.-Welfare can also provide you for free: food, safer sex products
(condoms, lube, dental damns), gloves, finger gloves, wet wipes, hand
sanitisers, lollipops, menstruation products &amp; non-judgmental
chats to resolve any problems you might have. They can also provide a
uber service if needed (please only use if really in need: we have a
limited amount of funds dedicated to this scheme). The welfare is a
fully queer, very diverse team of ravers that are trained and have seen
it all. There is also SIA security &amp; medics on site.Please
contact riposte.london@gmail.com or DM us on
https://www.instagram.com/riposte.london if you have any questionENTRY
REQUIREMENTS- This is an 18+ event- Valid form of PHYSICAL ID

entry (body search + bag) &amp; your ID will be scanned as in all

events.description:
\*\*Postponed until March - Due to Illness\*\*

\*\*Thursday February 29th (Will run in March)\*\*  
\*\*19.00 – 20.30, London UK (GMT)\*\*  
\*\*Lambeth Area\*\*

\*\*A live Transgender Portrait Photography Art Workshop\*\*

\*\*Have you ever wanted to know how to take great photos and understand
how to set up your shot so it looks amazing?\*\*

In our fourth at workshop, you will be guided by the wonderful Rebecca
as she shows us everything you need to know to take pictures like a pro.

\*\*Please note that due to limited equipment, we will be limiting this
workshop to 10 people only. First come first serve basis.\*\*

Further, as the materials needed for this workshop are quite expensive,
we will be \*\*charging £5 per person, which will be payable in
advance.\*\* (A link will be sent to you if you RSVP).

You will be guided step-by-step in the process of creating your own
amazing photos. No prior experience is required!

While you will be using professional gear while you learn about
lighting, composition and framing, there is also an opportunity for you
to take your own photos and leave with your own prints.

This is a fun and friendly environment helping you relax and connect
with your inner creative. This thoughtful, artistic activity can open up
the mind and relieve you of outside worries.

You do not need to bring anything apart from your lovely self. All
materials will be provided.

\*\*PLEASE NOTE: If you RSVP but find you cannot attend, please opt out
to make the space available for someone else as we will have a waiting
list.\*\*

\*\*Who this is for:\*\*  
Anyone who is transgender or supporting transgender and wants to do
something a little different. To enjoy themselves and take some down
time while expressing themselves through art. This is a friendly and
supportive environment where everyone, regardless of their artistic
abilities are welcome.

\*\*About Us:\*\*  
This event is part of a series of events run by the London Transgender
Meetup Group, sponsored by Lambeth Council and supported by LGBT Hero.

\### Sign Up Now To Secure Your Place

\*\*We will have to limit numbers to make sure that we can host the
event properly, so please RSVP now to avoid disappointment.\*\*

events.description:
[ ][1] [ TICKETS HERE ][2] All roads lead to Dalston on the 7th of March for ‘Unbound’, a raucous
evening of live performances and dazzling DJ sets to raise money for a
fabulous cause. Set yourself free with dancing, singing, and coming

celebrates unity between clothing, gender liberation, and identity
experimentation. 100% of the ticket sales will go to the charity.

***DJ set and general debauchery - 9pm onwards ***

 

*G(end)er Swap is a UK based LGBTQ+ style outreach organisation that
supports Trans+ people to access clothes, community and style resources.
Their core values are to minimise barriers for gender-diverse people to
experiment with their self-expression. G(end)er Swap equips individuals
with clothing, styling, makeup, and wellness resources and tools across
a plethora of platforms (both digitally and in person) via workshops,
pop ups, digital support initiatives, exhibitions and more. While we
endeavour to ensure the live performances are as accessible as possible

events.name: Transmissions presents: THE RASPBERRY REICH (2004)
events.description:
On night two of Queer As In Fuck U, we’ve joined forces with our
comrades at Tissue to bring you a rare screening of the legendary Bruce
LaBruce‘s delirious piece of hardcore agitprop, The Raspberry
Reich(2004). Taking their cues from the Baader-Meinhof Gang, a ragtag
gay militia kidnaps the son of a wealthy industrialist in order to
further their fight against fascism, heterosexuality, and bourgeoise
life. Radical, satirical, funny, and deliciously messed up, LaBruce’s
battlecry against respectability politics, censorship, and gay
assimilation plays like a punk rock song belted into a double-ended
dildo, and twenty years later it still demands to be seen.

Joining us to introduce the film will be writer, artist, and co-curator
at Tissue, Sam Moore.

Find us salivating in the bowels of Dalston Superstore for a work by one
of queer cinema’s greats.

“HETEROSEXUALITY IS THE OPIATE OF THE MASSES”

events.name: Transmissions presents: LOVE IS THE DEVIL (1998)
events.description:
Continuing our March season of bold, explicit, and uncompromising queer
cinema, Queer As In Fuck U, we’re proud to present underrated
masterpiece Love Is The Devil: Study For A Portrait of Francis Bacon
(1998). Director John Maybury – who first rose to prominence helming
music videos for Sinead O’Connor and Pet Shop Boys, as well as
collaborating with Derek Jarman – crafts not only a rigorous snapshot of
a period in iconic contemporary artist Francis Bacon‘s life, but a
vividly immersive journey into the dark heart of the work itself.

Love Is The Devil seems to live within Bacon’s brutal paintings,
depicting a cutthroat world of cruel figures and emotional depravity as
it depicts the fraught relationship between Bacon (Derek Jacobi) and his
troubled lover George Dyer (Daniel Craig), conjuring the gay pub culture
of 1960s London, and letting viewers float down a river of gruel and
into Bacon’s consciousness. Come for a hunky young Daniel Craig and
unforgettable cinematography by John Mathieson (Gladiator, Logan,
Hannibal), stay for a devilish supporting turn by Tilda Swinton and
polari insults delivered a mile a minute.

We’ll be cosy in the bowels of Dalston Superstore, ready for another
night at the movies designed for our beloved trans audience.

“Do I possess some inner destructive demon?”  

Tickets available via
OutSavvy: https://www.outsavvy.com/organiser/transmissions

Please note that this film deals with suicide and addiction.   Subtitles
will be displayed throughout the film.   Seating is a mixture of

first served.

Raghd

Raghd is rightfully being hailed as one of the most talented and
exciting new artists from Sweden. She blends rap, electronic dance, and
alternative rock into something completely its own. Carrying an
unapologetic punk energy, while showcasing incredible lyricism that is
vulnerable, humorous, smart, and playful, Raghd stands out as an
outstandingly versatile artist.

Venus Anon

Venus Anon has proven to be one of the most compelling artists in
today\'s contemporary music scene. She is of Iranian descent, and spent
her early years on the Swedish west coast listening to Googoosh and
Timbaland. During her teenage years, she lived in Stockholm and became
deeply embedded in the city\'s underground and queer scene, allowing
every encounter with new music to become an influence. Contemporary R&B,
clever pop productions, 21st-century emotional indie and future bass -
all can be heard as small traces in Venus Anon’s sound today.

events.name: Transmissions presents: ANATOMY OF HELL (2004)
events.description:
For the finale of our March season of bold, explicit, and uncompromising
queer cinema, Queer As In Fuck U, we’ve looked to one of the true
masters of provocation, France’s infamous auteur Catherine Breillat.
Anatomy of Hell (2004) chronicles four nights between a suicidally
depressed woman and the gay man she picks up at a club and pays to
“watch her when she is unwatchable”, observing her body, and hearing her
proclamations about sex, gender, and patriarchy.

Join us for this chic and at times shocking piece of arthouse mastery
that continues to polarise viewers who either see it as feminist or
unacceptably obscene. You be the judge.

“The woman is the man’s disease”    

Tickets available via
OutSavvy: https://www.outsavvy.com/organiser/transmissions

Please note that this film contains nudity and graphic depictions of
sex.   Subtitles will be displayed throughout the film.   Seating is a
mixture of benches, backed chairs, bar stools, and floor space, and is
first come, first served.

events.name: Seize the means: Staff Trans Healthcare fundraiser
events.description:
SEIZE THE MEANS OF MEDICAL TRANSITION! Dalston Superstore presents our
annual staff healthcare fundraiser for Trans Day of Visibility, with all
proceeds going to Superstore staff gender affirming funds. We need to
relinquish the idea that visibility is positive in and of itself. The
hyper visibility that trans\* people have experienced in the past decade
has left us increasingly vulnerable to violence from both the public and
the government while continuously being neglected by social services,
including the NHS. The increased exposure of trans\* people has not
improved our access to gender affirming health care. Rather, we are left
hanging with an expected waiting time of more than five years for an
initial appointment at the Gender Identity Clinic. Fundraisers and
privatised health care should not replace the public healthcare system
but for most trans\* people, this is currently our only option. Thus,
health care becomes a matter of proximity to privilege. We as trans\*
people should get to define for ourselves whether and how we choose to
transition medicially, legally and socially. On this Trans Day of
In/visibility, we encourage you to seize the means of medical transition
to redistribute resources, including but not limited to money, HRT, and
knowledge. Dalston Superstore is throwing a fundraising party to support
gender affirming health care for our trans members of staff. This party
centres trans\* people, medicalised and otherwise.

We’ll be taking donations on the door and inside all night, come open
your hearts and wallets in support of trans\* healthcare.

Minimum Donation £7. Door Policy

events.name: Transmissions presents: DESIGN FOR LIVING (1933)
events.description:
For our April season at Transmissions, we’ll be exploring the mechanics
of the triangle, and looking at what happens when there’s love to go
around. In Three’s Company: Polyamory, Throuples, and Unethical
Non-Mongamy we’ll take you on a journey from tenderqueer housing drama,
to couples falling for a third, to steamy mind games, and women who just
can’t choose between boyfriends. It’s all fun and games until somebody
gets hurt, or perhaps the hurt is being laid down by societal pressure
and heteronormative ideas about what a relationship should look like?
Whatever the case, these cinematic trios never take the easy route, and
you’ll want to be there for their every move.

On opening night we’re serving up a pre-code classic from Ernst Lubitsch
about a crazy gal and her two pals, Design For Living (1933). Can a
modern woman really have it all? And if she wants one man just as much
as the other, does she really have to choose? Come find out when we
screen a surprisingly modern film from a time before the word “polycule”
began plaguing our every waking moment.

We’ll be deep in the warm embrace of the basement at Dalston Superstore,
ready to invite you in.

“Immorality may be fun, but it isn’t fun enough to take the place of one
hundred percent virtue and three square meals a day.”

Tickets available via
OutSavvy: https://www.outsavvy.com/organiser/transmissions

Subtitles will be displayed throughout the film. Seating is a mixture of
benches, backed chairs, bar stools, and floor space, and is first come,
first served.

events.name: Writing for Performance workshops with Liv Ello
events.description:
A 5-part ‘writing for performance’ weekly workshop series, providing a
safe space for emerging writers to develop their ideas through writing
tools and techniques with room for experimenting and break away from
convention. A space to write share and develop without the pressure of
producing something at the end of the series, but rather a focus on
skill development, community building and finding your voice through
writing. 

This workshop series is run by writer and performer, Liv Ello (Body
Show, SWARM, Jack the Mack, director of Frankie Thompson: CAttS).

This workshop series is aimed to create an encouraging environment to
explore your ideas through writing exercises, discussion and support to
develop your writing skills and become confident in your writing
abilities.  
  
The sessions are catered towards anyone of any writing experience,
whether you’re an experienced playwright, curious about developing text
for your performance practice, love the idea of writing something new
every session or absolutely terrified by it!  
  
The aim of this course is to use writing for performance as a creative
tool for developing our ideas, not just as the thing that formalises
them at the end. It’s writing for discovery and expression, not just
definition.

The course is designed so that if you can only afford a single drop-in
session, you will still come away with valuable tools and explorations,
whilst those completing the full course will also experience a sense of
progression and development

cabaret and music from some of our most delicious t\'ARTs.

 [ tickets ][1] We have invited some of our favourite performers to entertain you all,
at a night that will be nothing short of t\'ARTopian.

t’ART is a queer-led arts and lit collective, that creates space (on the

*Let\'s get mouth-watering*

Performers: 

Alexis Sakellaris - Musical Comedy

Alexis (@alexis\_sakellaris) is a queer international artist who
graduated from Mountview last year and hasn’t had a stable routine
since. His first foray into original work, A STAN IS BORN! is a musical
comedy about how he devolved into a lil gay stan obsessed with pop divas
after a drastic move from NYC to rural Germany. This chaotic mess of a
show is heading to several London venues and Edinburgh Fringe this
summer, which is just like… wild lol.

Phil from Venus - Poetry

 Phil is a writer, actor and photographer. He likes to dress his
rambling thoughts with flowery language, calling it poetry! When
reading, the audience is urged to join in, making it a conversation
where authenticity reigns - the room becomes his mind and we all reside
in it, becoming his sounding board and sometimes, voice of reason.

Amy Lynne Westray - Drag

Amy Lynne Westray (they/she) is a queer theatre maker, cabaret artist
& facilitator with particular love for clowning, drag, physical
theatre, music & spoken word poetry.  They studied European Theatre
Arts a heavily ensemble & devising based course. Since graduating
last year, they co-founded a clowning and cabaret company Curls N Swirls

events.name: XOXA NYC TAKEOVER
events.description:
NYC based collective XOXA make their London debut with a full takeover
of Dalston Superstore. This collision of two legendary city’s queer
underground scenes will be iconic.  Upstairs is giving pure queer
utopian joy with London’s favorites UOKHUN (RITA LIN b2b Victoria
Peckham) and Queer House Party residents Harry Gay, Passer and Watcha
with a closing set by XOXA’s Kandylion. Hosts and dancers Bolly-Illusion
and Taali will captivate the bar area bringing the high queer energy
that London’s party scene is known for. Downstairs in the rave cave get
lost in a recreation of a NYC queer dance floor with XOXA residents
Panooc and Kandylion (coming all the way from NYC) pulling from their
extensive music collections of east coast house, acid and vocal house.
These two seasoned DJs who have inspired and turned up dance floors all
over New York for years with their high energy and heart pumping dance
music. Joining them is London’s own Reece Spooner – a Balamii resident
whose genre fluid sets are the perfect embodiment of NYC’s diverse dance
floor sound. From jackin’ house, acid and techno to ghetto, jersey club,
electro, UK bass, breakbeat, footwork and modern-day rave, his palette
is wide, heady and leans nicely on the anthems. XOXA is a platform,
party and DJ collective based out of NYC with a worldwide reach. Their
mission is to support and highlight artists in the electronic music
scene while providing an intentional space for dancers and partygoers.
XOXA works closely with DJs spanning genres, scenes, countries and
backgrounds all with the common goal of uplifting and unifying
marginalized artists. £8 before 11 / £10 after

events.name: Queer Running Club
events.description:
The most important thing you should know about QRC if you are planning
to attend is that this is a community. A decentralised space for us all,
as queer-identifying people, to run together without judgment or fear.

We are a friendly crew, we always have a drink after so that we can
socialise as well. Sessions are normally one hour long, they vary each
week.

It will be a mixture of a long run (up to 8km), hill sprints, paced
runs, and sprints or running games. We don\'t have a specific pace that
you need to run at, ALL levels are welcome. If you can comfortably run
5km you will get more from the runs. Some sessions have two people and
some have twenty, but, we always try to stay together.

events.name: Transmissions presents: X Y AND ZEE (1972)
events.description:
You’ll never believe how some folks live. For London socialites Robert
(Michael Caine) and Zee (a blistering Elizabeth Taylor), love is a cruel
game, and sex is little more than a weapon. But when Robert’s latest
affair with young single mum Stella (Susannah York) begins, it’s all out
war and the venomous Zee will stop at nothing to get even. And god help
anyone who gets in their way.

Don’t miss a film that plays like the psychedelic sibling of Who’s
Afraid of Virginia Woolf? when we screen the scandalous, acerbic, and
unbelievably gaggy X Y and Zee (1972) on night three of Three’s Company:
Polyamory, Throuples, and Unethical Non-Mongamy. Find us cosy in the
basement at Dalston Superstore, ready for a motion picture about lovers
on their very worst behaviour.   “I wasn’t being vicious, was I?”

Tickets available via
OutSavvy: https://www.outsavvy.com/organiser/transmissions

Subtitles will be displayed throughout the film. Seating is a mixture of
benches, backed chairs, bar stools, and floor space, and is first come,
first served.

events.name: Cum As U Are
events.description: [ TICKETS ][1] **✨**Unleash your inner flirt and join us for a night of silly sex positivity ✨  This is a sex positive night all about feeling good and turning yourself on, expect irresistible cabaret performances and sultry tunes throughout the evening Celebrating self-expression in all its glorious forms, our line up promises to blend feel good rhythms with heartfelt live performance.  Doors 19:00 Performances begin 19:45 LAST ENTRY 22:30 End 00:00 No one turned away for lack of funds, please email [rainagreifer@gmail.com](mailto:rainagreifer@gmail.com), no questions asked. We will be providing a fully detailed content warnings document closer to the date but please be aware that the evening will include poetry and performances on the topic of sex. We also have a dedicated accessibility coordinator who can be contacted prior to the event, should any customers need anything to be arranged in advance. Their email is rainagreifer@gmail.com ### The Lineup Raina Greifer (Host) They/She Raina Greifer (she/they) is a Bristol-based theatre maker and producer interested in exploring themes around sex, consent, and grief.  They were shortlisted for the SH24: Sexual Health Awards 2022 as Young Person of the Year and were a BBC Words First Finalist in 2021.  Her solo show MANIC won Best Solo Show at Fuse International in 2022.  Raina loves talking about being horny.  She loves being dramatic about it. Rosa Garland Rosa is a clown, writer and burlesque artist. She likes things that are sticky, sexy and stupid. Her queer cult hit show TRASH SALAD has sold out at Soho Theatre, Edinburgh Fringe and VAULT Festival where it was nominated for the 2023 Innovation Award. She is currently developing a new show, Primal Bog. Maedb Joy Maedb Joy is a poet, writer and theatre maker, making work about class, sex work, queerness and womanhood. She is alumni of Guildhall School of Music and Drama (rated 1st in the UK for arts + drama), and the Royal Court Playwriting Group. Maedb is the founder and and artistic director of Sexquisite Events, a performing arts company platforming sex worker artists across theatre, cabaret and nightlife across the UK. She is also the co-founder of Riot Party, a sex positive queer community producing sold out club nights in London and Manchester. Both organisations are committed to creating paid creative opportunities for sex workers, and impacting meaningful change through art and entertainment. BEKIMACHINE BEKIMACHINE is a London-born, Midlands based emerging producer & DJ. She DJs progressive/melodic house & techno, peak-time/driving techno & hard techno.  She\'s known for producing electronic music ranging from synth pop to techno, creating an ethereal, otherworldly sound. She has a habit of crafting music with a sense of atonality, filled with catchy melodies and bass hooks whilst evoking nostalgia.   In 2022 she took DJing from Twitch to the stage, playing a string of shows to date including TwitchCon Amsterdam, Berlin Brighton & Shaydefest - falling in love with the atmosphere & energy of the live room, whilst sending the audience on an emotional journey through music. In 2023, she opened up for Elevation at EGG London as their DJ competition winner, as well as playing shows for Shaydefest, Deep Underground Notts and the Junc Collective.  2023 marked a new chapter in her music, exploring techno and trance in her sound. Her latest single, The Void (Chaotic Evil Remix) has seen radio play on BBC Radio 1 Introducing Dance. Prior to this, she released her debut album Another Atmosphere in 2022, a video-game inspired synth pop saga, gaining positive support from SIDE-LINE Magazine and securing radio play from BBC Introducing. Aria Progressive house producer Aria finds inspiration in the freedom and escapism that music brings. Her ethereal melodies take you away to another world, to your true reality. Let her take you on a journey from beautiful melodic waters to deeper tech progresive house that will have you in a trance. M Hunny South london based Brummie, M Hunny mixes her love for garage & electronic music with a distinct 90s and early 2000s sound. With a monthly show on Voices radio playing an eclectic mix of genres, M Hunny has also played at Ministry of Sound & recently opened up for Children of Zeus. Co-founder & designer at Barbara Bianco the DJ merges the worlds of fashion & music putting on nights showcasing talent from around the UK and dressing everyone in BB. Stay locked in for female vocals, bass heavy bangers and addictive hooks. Fanny Bleach Fanny Bleack is a raucous and riotous comedy act, in 2023 Fanny stormed the stage to be crowned the winner of East London’s Top of the Slops Season 3! Promising to be a sexy and filthy act, Fanny Bleach is a drag thing not to miss [1]: https://www.outsavvy.com/event/18479/cum-as-u-are

events.name: NO HARD SHOULDER
events.description:
[ TICKETS HERE ][1] United by a passion for resurrecting the raw energy and authenticity of
the underground music scene from the 1990s, a collective of DJs from the
East London music scene is the driving force behind NO HARD SHOULDER.

Fuelled by a love for tech and deep house, minimal tech, breaks, and
techno, these artists have banded together to create unforgettable
experiences in intimate club settings.

Drawing inspiration from the gritty, electric atmosphere of the \'90s
rave culture, each member brings their own unique style and influences
to the dancefloor, creating diverse sonic landscapes that keep the crowd
on their toes all night long.

But it\'s not just about the music; it\'s about fostering a sense of
community and connection among like-minded individuals who share a deep
appreciation for electronic music. Whether you\'re a seasoned raver or a
newcomer to the scene, you\'re welcomed with open arms at these parties.

In an era dominated by mainstream trends and commercialism, NO HARD
SHOULDER offers a refreshing change, and welcomes the most diverse of
crowds. So if you find yourself craving an escape from the ordinary,
keep an eye out for their next event.

events.name: One More Time
events.description:
[ TICKETS ][1] Encore Une Fois - after a short break, One More Time is BACK!

Its 1997 and Girl Power is everywhere! The Spice Girls dominate the
charts, Louise, Dannii Minogue and Gina G fly the flag for the pop
girls. Katrina and The Waves won Eurovision, Janet Jackson returned and
All Saints, Natalie Imbruglia and Shola Ama launched.

The boys were busy too though with Backstreet Boys, 911, Boyzone,
Hanson, North & South, No Mercy and Five all making the top 10.
Robbie Williams launched his solo career proper, Kavana adorned bedroom
walls and Will Smith was the man in black. Not content with the charts
being full of pure pop, Texas, Republica and No Doubt added some guitars
to the mix. 1997 also saw HUGE dance anthems from Gala (and her
trombelese), Ultra Nate and Dario G - not to mention the trio of hits
from Sash! And just as the year was ending, we said hello to bright new
things Steps and Aqua!

We’ll be playing the A list popstars from 1997 along with B listers like
Michelle Gayle, Lisa Stansfield and Skunk Anansie along with loads of
other pop and dance hits from 1997. Immerse yourself with memorabilia
galore from 1997 adorning our walls including our much loved chart wall
whilst our resident drag queen Karma will be back with a homage to
1997. 

Expect loads of forgotten gems you\'re unlikely to hear anywhere else
(from Jimmy Ray to The Course and Clock). Our Bargain Bin first hour of
1997’s pop flops (from Mary Kiani to Newton and \*\*whisper \*\* Kylie
Minogue - yes it was that year) kicks the night off as usual from 9pm.



[1]: https://www.outsavvy.com/event/19001/one-more-time-1997

events.description:
On closing night of Three’s Company: Polyamory, Throuples, and Unethical
Non-Mongamy we screen Professor Marston and the Wonder Women (2017), an
endearing gem from director Angela Robinson (D.E.B.S.) that tells the
true story of the inventor of Wonder Woman, and his polyamorous
relationship with the two women who inspired the character. Far from
fading into the background, the women behind the man are as much the
context of the story as he is, and their love for each other during a
time where acceptance defied imagination is an integral part of the
film’s emotional foundation. Luke Evans, Rebecca Hall, and Bella
Heathcote star in a story of censorship, repression, and forbidden love
against a backdrop of 1940s America.

and extremely horny origins of a comic-book icon. Whatever your
pleasure, you’ll find us cosy in the basement at Dalston Superstore for
another night curated especially for our beloved trans audience.

live it?”

events.description:
In May, multi-talented hurricane, creator of the infamous Kate Cobain
powerpoint, and the other mind behind Transmissions, Heather Estradiol
(@djungelskog\_gf) is back at the reigns for a whole month of lesbian
larceny, sapphic supremacy, and extreme yearning. From elaborate heists,
to cyber crime, espionage, murder most foul, and devious dealings done
in style, these ladies are simply up to no good. Will they get the bag
and get away with it, or will love get in the way? Join us every week to
find out, and celebrate a mantra many hold dear: be gay, do crime.

On opening night we screen the ultra-slick Ocean’s 8 (2018). Far from
just the girlbossification of Soderbergh, it offers a certain hit that
only a movie with this stacked a cast and this big a boner for bad girls
could. Sexual tension and unspoken history simmer between Sandra Bullock
and Cate Blanchett‘s characters as they lead a gang of women through a
plan to steal a very expensive necklace full of diamonds from round Anne
Hathaway’s neck at the MET Gala. Rihanna, Sarah Paulson, Mindy Kaling,
and more co-star in a sleek, sexy romp that we just can’t stop coming
back to.

Not gay enough for you? Wait till you hear about Sandy’s rumoured
private member’s club. Join us downstairs at Dalston Superstore for
another night at the movies by and for London’s trans community.

“Somewhere out there is an eight-year-old girl lying in bed, dreaming of
being a criminal. Let’s do this for her.”

events.name: Comedy Night: John Tothill and Will Owen (WIPs)
events.description:
[ TICKETs ][1] Two Edinburgh WIPs from rising comedy stars John Tothill and Will Owen!

**John Tothill: Thank God This Lasts Forever (Work in Progress)**

Last year, John Tothill was visited by a series of terrible plagues.
Now, he\'s desperate to tell you all about it (preferably over many
drinks and maybe the tiniest cigarette?). Imagine the Old Testament,
with less historical accuracy and even more divine intervention. And
it\'s a stand-up show, not a book. Chortle Awards\' Best Newcomer
nominee 2024. John\'s debut show was one of the Best-Reviewed Edinburgh
Fringe Shows of 2023 ([Comedy.co.uk][2]). As seen on Comedy Central
Live. \'Resplendent, ridiculous, didactic, and fabulous\' (*Tatler*).

*\*\*\*\*\* EdFest*

*\*\*\*\*1⁄2 Chortle*

*\*\*\*\* Guardian*

*\*\*\*\* Telegraph*

*\*\*\*\* Skinny*

**Will Owen: Like, Nobody\'s Watching (Work in Progress)**

Watch rising star Will Owen fight for his place in the hearts of the
Great British Public, in a competition entirely of his own-making. From
the Winner of Leicester Square New Comedian of the Year comes a
glittering debut comedy hour of fastidiously-curated spontaneity.
Featuring admittedly over-developed musings on popularity, performance
and the Pussycat Dolls. He will dance like nobody’s watching, just as
long as somebody is. The stakes *have* been higher. Bath Comedy Festival
New Comedian Second Runner-Up 2022; 2Northdown Finalist 2022.

‘a master of the casually cruel comment, biting yet delivered with an
archetypal Gen Z indifference… it’s a winning formula\' (*Chortle*)

Directed by Daniel Emery and Molly Stacey. 



[1]: https://www.outsavvy.com/event/19336/queer-comedy-night-john-tothill-and-will-owen-wips
[2]: http://comedy.co.uk/

events.name: Transmissions presents: KAJILLIONAIRE (2020):
events.description:
From programmer Heather Estradiol and indie darling Miranda July comes a
sweet and strange story about a young woman (bicon Evan Rachel Wood) who
finds her world turned upside down when her criminal parents invite an
outsider (Gina Rodriguez) to join them on the major heist they’re
planning. The complications of a peculiar upbringing, neurodivergence,
and budding romance all throw a spanner in the works and result in a
film that is by turns funny, affecting, and beautiful.   Join us
downstairs at Dalston Superstore for night two of Crimes of Passion:
Criminal Dykes, this one’s a charmer.   “Most happiness comes from dumb
things.”  

Tickets available via
OutSavvy: https://www.outsavvy.com/organiser/transmissions

Subtitles will be displayed throughout the film. Seating is a mixture of
benches, backed chairs, bar stools, and floor space, and is first come,
first served.

[ TICKETS ][1] Choked Up! Is a brand spanking new night for all your scratch night
itches, if you’re into that kind of thing. 

Our debut night is a chance to catch the first ever screening of Good
Grief! A film by host and choreographer, Daze Hingorani, exploring the
intersections of queerness and grief and how joyful it is to love
anything enough that you miss it that much.

secret third act, it’s the first of many nights where we’ll be
platforming new works by outstanding performers. 

Doors will open at 7pm for a swift start of 7:30pm for performances,
there’ll be plenty of breaks for drinks and kisses and even a Q&A
for all the behind the scenes gossip of the making of Good Grief!

events.name: Thursday Social Drinks In Soho
events.description:
Join me and your fellow trans lovelies for a relaxed meetup which takes
place on the second \*\*Thursday of the month in the Soho, central
London area.\*\*

This place has a great buzz. It\'s a sneaky way to start the weekend
early. Come and join us :)

\*\*RSVP NOW\*\*

We have a private area upstairs in the venue, which is plenty of space
for us all to chat, hear each other and relax.

Thursday is the new start of the weekend. Let\'s use this opportunity to
make some new friends and chat about whatever pleases you.  
This event will suit you if you are new to attending the meetup or are
one of our wonderful regulars. It is a popular evening with lots of
different people popping in. There is no need to be nervous. We are all
very friendly and welcoming. You\'ll feel right at home. :)

\*\*What is this meetup?\*\*  
This is a relaxed, friendly and inclusive meetup for the trans people of
London. This is an opportunity to make new friends and chat over a
sneaky Thursday drink.

\*\*Who is it for?\*\*  
Everyone from the trans community is welcome. This is an opportunity to
be yourself, whatever you identify as. We are inclusive and happy to
welcome you.

\*\*How does it work?\*\*  
All you have to do is RSVP and then we will message you on the day with
the event location. Then, all you have to do is show up.

We will make sure that you meet some new people and get a chance to get
to know your fellow trans buddies. This event is very friendly and will
welcome you and make sure you feel comfortable and happy.  
It is free to attend, just buy yourself a drink at the bar.

\*\*Please Note:\*\* RSVP is a must as the location (based around Soho)
will be sent by email on the day to those who have RSVP\'d only. RSVP
closes at 16.00 on the day of the event.

\*\*RSVP NOW\*\*

events.name: Transmissions presents: D.E.B.S. (2004):
events.description:
Always wished Charlie’s Angels was just that little bit gayer? Or
watched films like Legally Blonde and wished the girls kissed? On night
three of Crimes of Passion: Criminal Dykes, Heather Estradiol has just
the film for you.

Directed by Angela Robinson (Professor Marston and the Wonder Women),
D.E.B.S. (2004) follows a team of international teenage super spies who
are put at odds when one of their members falls for the enemy. Will she
stay loyal to the firm or follow her heart? It’s the question on
everyone’s mind in a classic full of B Movie charms and bubblegum
visuals, a quintessentially 2000s piece of queer cinema about girls,
guns, and going gay for your nemesis.

Stars Devon Aoki, Jordana Brewster, Meagan Goode, Jimmi Simpson, Holland
Taylor, and more.

Join us at headquarters in the basement of Dalston Superstore for
another night at the movies.   “The only brave thing I’ve done this
whole time is what I’m doing now.”  

Tickets available via
OutSavvy: https://www.outsavvy.com/organiser/transmissions

Subtitles will be displayed throughout the film. Seating is a mixture of
benches, backed chairs, bar stools, and floor space, and is first come,
first served.

events.description:
Your favorite queer rave baby is turning six! And in celebration we’re
inviting all our shawties to come party like it’s our birthday, because
this time it actually is!  In the lazerpit festivities will be dedicated
to showcasing Pumping Velvet’s immaculate residents. Starting the night

from an extended Asia tour is our fabulous headliner Joe Delon. Joe’s
sets represent everything we hold dear about dancing music at PV,
drawing on the fundamentals of dance music’s past – the snap of a disco
break, the sleaze of a Chicago bassline, and the bittersweet touch of

pure pop catharsis along the way. Upstairs sees a wavy night of music as
M.Kwas and Edith Escobar step up with sets bound to span bashment,
garage and pop, while Kunteaa showcases her roots in black queer culture
with everything from ballroom to grime to baile funk. Come find us in
the club with a bottle bub and PUMP SOME VELVET.
