events.description:
[ TICKETS ][1] Right, Year Three. Listening ears, please.

Today you are SO LUCKY, because your former teacher, Mrs Lisa Lakeside
(John Tothill), has (out of the KINDNESS of her heart) organised a Very
Special Comedy Show.

On 19th May at VFDalston, she will be hosting an INCREDIBLE line-up of
comedy acts (to be announced), and you are going to listen POLITELY to
what they have to say. Remember: they are giving up their time and you
are representing the school, so I know I can TRUST YOU to be sensible.

events.name: Long Live Queer Nightlife, a FREE community event.
events.description:
[ RSVP here ][1] **Long Live Queer Night Life **

**7 pm Doors **

**7.30 pm Start / Three sections of 20 minutes with 10-minute reset
breaks. **

A panel discussion with author Amin Ghaziani, Phoebe Patey-Ferguson, and
Kat Hudson will be hosted by Lyall Hakaraia. Talks of the establishment
of VFDs activation **Femmetopia**, which encouraged queer disrupters in
East London to tear down the patriarchy and celebrate diversity beyond
the heteronormative.  We will explore the wider themes of change
recorded in the book and finish with a Q and A. 

**9 pm to 9.20 pm performance and then dancing till 11 pm.**  
Following the discussion there will be cabaret performances from QTIPOC
artist Rhys\'s Pieces, then dancing until late. 

**Please RSVP so we can reserve you a spot !**  
 

You can also buy the book ‘Long Live Queer Night Life’ published by
Princeton University Press at the event and signed by the author Amin
Ghaziani at an incredibly discounted rate of £15.  
  
**Amin Ghaziani** 

The book: In this exhilarating journey into underground parties,
pulsating with life and limitless possibility, Acclaimed author Amin
Ghaziani unveils the unexpected revolution revitalizing urban nightlife.

Far from the gay bar with its largely white, gay male clientele, here is
a dazzling scene of secret parties— club nights—wherein culture
creatives, many of whom are queer, trans, and racial minorities, reclaim
the night in the name of those too long left out. Episodic, nomadic, and
radically inclusive, club nights are refashioning queer nightlife in
boundlessly imaginative and powerfully defiant ways.

@amin\_ghaziani @princetonupress

**Dr Phoebe Patey-Ferguson** is an academic, artist and producer. Their
research expertise is on international theatre festivals, rooted in the
Sociology of Theatre and Performance. This work frequently intersects
with their further research interests in live art, contemporary British
theatre, and queer theory. 

Phoebe is the course leader of the world\'s first MA in Queer
Performance training students to create, explore, examine and expand
queer performance practice.

@ppateyferg

**Kat Hudson Katherine \'Kat\' Hudson** is a multimedia artist and
writer who works closely with archives and libraries. Kat has curated
notable community-focused exhibitions and nightlife events and lives and
works in London, England.  
@kathudson\_  
Kat\'s personal art practice explores individual multiplicity,
collaborative creation, community wellbeing and performing utopia
through drawing, painting, collage and sound. Her curatorial practice
explores queer intersectional feminism, the work of her peers and
subcultural art and nightlife movements in London.

**Lyall Hakaraia** is a QTBIPOC Maori artist and Takatapui Rangatira
queer community organiser who runs the queer art spaces  VFD over two
venues in Dalston . A parent to our beloved daughter Tui and a raft of
fish, birds and two black cats.

@lyallhakaraia

**Rhys Pieces  **is a gender-f\*cking cabaret creature! A one-stop
cabaret troupe, multitalented, multi-award winning messy, smelly,
fabulous, and putting on a show! They are the creator and host of
@QueerdosCabaret and have toured the world shaking their pieces! 

@RhyssPieces\_





[1]: https://www.outsavvy.com/event/20184/long-live-queer-nightlife-a-free-community-event

events.name: Transmissions presents: TOM OF FINLAND (2017)
events.description:
This month at Transmissions, the team behind HARDER: A Season of Lesbian
Kink is back for a second June of hot and heavy curation for our beloved
crowd of trans people of taste, and basement dwelling perverts. Runner
up of Bootblack Europe 2024, Butch Boots (Riposte, Pop-Up Dyke Bar) is
becoming a fixture in the London scene, with its creator Astrid Johnson
taking her bespoke bootblacking and leathercare services to some of the
hottest events in town. Lucky for us, she’ll be in residence for four
nights tracing the history of leather faggotry on screen, showcasing
shorts by the iconic Kenneth Anger, William Friedkin’s monumental
classic Cruising, rare documentary High Shine, and more.

But before all that, we screen Tom of Finland (2017), a celebratory
biopic of Touko Laaksonen, an artist whose legendary homoerotic
illustrations bloomed amidst the oppression of the 1950s, capturing
existing subcultures and influencing those that would follow. Join us
for a tribute to the life and work of a pioneering queer artist, whose
subversion has proved immortal.

“Everybody should see your drawings”

Tickets available via
OutSavvy: https://www.outsavvy.com/organiser/transmissions

Subtitles will be displayed throughout the film. Seating is a mixture of
benches, backed chairs, bar stools, and floor space, and is first come,
first served.

events.name: Thursday Social Drinks In Soho
events.description:
Join me and your fellow trans lovelies for a relaxed meetup which takes
place on the second \*\*Thursday of the month in the Soho, central
London area.\*\*

This place has a great buzz. It\'s a sneaky way to start the weekend
early. Come and join us :)

\*\*RSVP NOW\*\*

We have a private area upstairs in the venue, which is plenty of space
for us all to chat, hear each other and relax.

Thursday is the new start of the weekend. Let\'s use this opportunity to
make some new friends and chat about whatever pleases you.  
This event will suit you if you are new to attending the meetup or are
one of our wonderful regulars. It is a popular evening with lots of
different people popping in. There is no need to be nervous. We are all
very friendly and welcoming. You\'ll feel right at home. :)

\*\*What is this meetup?\*\*  
This is a relaxed, friendly and inclusive meetup for the trans people of
London. This is an opportunity to make new friends and chat over a
sneaky Thursday drink.

\*\*Who is it for?\*\*  
Everyone from the trans community is welcome. This is an opportunity to
be yourself, whatever you identify as. We are inclusive and happy to
welcome you.

\*\*How does it work?\*\*  
All you have to do is RSVP and then we will message you on the day with
the event location. Then, all you have to do is show up.

We will make sure that you meet some new people and get a chance to get
to know your fellow trans buddies. This event is very friendly and will
welcome you and make sure you feel comfortable and happy.  
It is free to attend, just buy yourself a drink at the bar.

\*\*Please Note:\*\* RSVP is a must as the location (based around Soho)
will be sent by email on the day to those who have RSVP\'d only. RSVP
closes at 16.00 on the day of the event.

\*\*RSVP NOW\*\*

events.name: Transmissions presents: CRUISING (1980) + LEATHER (1996)
events.description:
Round three of Butch Boots‘ residence at Transmissions brings a rare
short, and an all-time classic to our humble basement screen. William
Friedkin (The Exorcist, Sorcerer) reached a great many heights in his
storied career, but perhaps the filmmaker’s most fascinating achievement
is Cruising (1980), a dark and seductive thriller starring Al Pacino as
a NYC cop sent undercover to find a serial killer targeting men in the
city’s underground of gay kink, where he must disappear into the fetish
clubs, meat markets, and cruising grounds that populate the night-time
landscape. Whether he’ll survive, and if he’ll still be the same person
if he does, remains to be seen.

Throughout it’s production in 1979, Cruising was dogged by protestors
from New York’s gay community who believed the piece to be so homophobic
that there were numerous elaborate disruptions during filming, which
continued upon theatrical release. But despite the controversy of the
day, Friedkin’s film has only become more and more beloved in subsequent
years by queer audiences who have found it impossible not to appreciate
its nuances, grime, and invaluable nature as a time capsule of the
leather scene.

“There’s a lot you don’t know about me.”

Before Cruising, not only you can join us for a screening of Hardy
Haberman‘s documentary short Leather (1996), which captures testimonies
from various leather lovers on the freedom found in the dynamics of
BDSM, you’ll also be able to purchase custom leather pieces by Dalston
royalty Malwina, ranging from cuffs, to studded bracelets, to harnesses
and more.

Find all this downstairs at Dalston Superstore, it’s gonna be quite a
night.

Tickets available via
OutSavvy: https://www.outsavvy.com/organiser/transmissions

Subtitles will be displayed throughout the film. Seating is a mixture of
benches, backed chairs, bar stools, and floor space, and is first come,
first served.

BOOTBLACK (2015) + LIVE BOOTBLACK DEMONSTRATION
events.description:
The finale of Butch Boots‘ residency at Transmissions brings you a rare
screening of High Shine: 15 Years of International Ms Bootblack (2015),
Christina K. Court‘s documentary which lovingly chronicles the history
and passion behind over a decade of community, and competitive
bootblacking. Informative, erotic, joyous, funny, and memorable, High
Shine gives viewers access to a wealth of collective knowledge on the
role of women in the leather scene, as well as voices that go far beyond
the white, cis archetype of the leather man.

“Sometimes activism comes in a tin of boot polish.”

After the film, the creator of Butch Boots (Riposte, Pop-Up Dyke Bar)
will be giving a live demonstration and sharing her own knowledge of
leathercare with our lucky audience members.

Join us deep down in the basement of Dalston Superstore, for an extra
special edition of Transmissions, a night by and for London’s trans
community.

events.name: Rishi Sunak\'s Leaving Drinks: Huck Magazine + Queer House Party
events.description:
ALL PROFITS GO TO SUPPORTING PALESTINIAN CAUSES It’s been 14 very long
years of Conservative party rule. Five Prime Ministers, four elections,
one referendum, countless scandals, a pandemic, an historic cost of
living crisis, over a decade of cuts to basic services, welfare and
social support, with over 330,000 deaths associated with them. A country
that, many would argue, has been broken – we can only hope not beyond
repair. Many of us have marched, fought, campaigned and tried to. Those
responsible, among them our current Prime Minister Rishi Sunak, look
finally set to be handed their marching orders in just a few short
weeks. If polls are to be believed the 4th of July will be the final day
of Sunak’s premiership and we thought we should send arguably the
richest man to ever be elected to Parliament off in style. There is no
place we’d rather get together and collectively scream “good riddance”
than in the hallowed hall (basement) of Dalston Superstore. Starting
from 9pm on 4 July, we’ll be screening the election results live, going
late into the night with an incredible roster of DJs curated by our good
friends Queer House Party. Huck’s Digital Editor and resident
gobshite Ben Smoke will be on hand to keep us abreast of developments
through the early hours, as we watch and celebrate (hopefully) the
demise of so many of those who have brought misery to millions. Don’t
tell anyone but we may also have a few extra surprises lined up for you
on the night… Of course, what comes next is not set. Indeed, even if
Keir Starmer, leader of the Labour Party does become the next Prime
Minister, as it looks likely he will, the fight both at home and abroad
is far from over. It’s why we’re taking the opportunity to fundraise for
those currently at the centre of a genocide that many say
Starmer provided political cover for. All profits from the night will be
going directly to organisations at the heart of providing vital
humanitarian assistance to those in Gaza. We are still a few weeks out
from the night and we’ll be doing a full line-up and beneficiary reveal
in the run up to the event over on our socials so be sure to follow if
you don’t already! THERE ARE NO ADVANCED TICKETS so you’ll need to get
there early, particularly if you want to join in our epic exit poll
celebration at 10pm. As extra incentive (as if you need any?!), we’ll be
giving away free copies of Huck 75, with legend Zarah Sultana on the
cover to the first 100 people through the door! It’s been a hard,
unrelenting few years – a simultaneously frantic and extraordinarily
dull election campaign, and an uncertain future awaits us all but on 4
July, let’s all get together to celebrate, to take the night to think of
all we’ve lost, all we’ve achieved and all we’re yet to win. To connect,
to laugh, to \[redacted\], and, most importantly, to (hopefully!!) say a
big SEE YA to the tories. See you all on the dancefloor x

events.name: Transmissions presents: A HISTORY OF VIOLENCE (2005)
events.description:
Night two of Mothers, Fathers, Daughters, Sons sees the return of
maestro and Transmissions favourite David Cronenberg (Crash, Videodrome,
eXistenZ) to our humble screen as we proudly present his visceral and
affecting blood-stained melodrama A History of Violence (2005). A deep
cut from Cronenberg‘s oeuvre but one which can easily hold its own
against his very best work, the film stars Viggo Mortensen as the
mild-mannered manager of a small town diner whose quiet life explodes
after a heroic act leads to revelations about the secret past he thought
he had outrun, putting everything he cares about at risk. Maria Bello,
Ed Harris, and William Hurt head up a superb supporting cast in a story
of family, forgiveness, and reconciling who we were with who we hope to
be. Don’t miss this emotional heavyweight from one of cinema’s greatest
directors. “Ask him, how come he’s so good at killing people?” Tickets
available via OutSavvy: https://www.outsavvy.com/organiser/transmissions
Please be aware that this film contains scenes of very strong violence.
Subtitles will be displayed throughout the film. Seating is a mixture of
benches, backed chairs, bar stools, and floor space, and is first come,
first served.

Join me and your fellow trans lovelies for a relaxed meetup which takes
place on the second \*\*Thursday of the month in the Soho, central
London area.\*\*

This place has a great buzz. It\'s a sneaky way to start the weekend
early. Come and join us :)

We have a private area upstairs in the venue, which is plenty of space
for us all to chat, hear each other and relax.

Thursday is the new start of the weekend. Let\'s use this opportunity to
make some new friends and chat about whatever pleases you.  
This event will suit you if you are new to attending the meetup or are
one of our wonderful regulars. It is a popular evening with lots of
different people popping in. There is no need to be nervous. We are all
very friendly and welcoming. You\'ll feel right at home. :)

\*\*What is this meetup?\*\*  
This is a relaxed, friendly and inclusive meetup for the trans people of
London. This is an opportunity to make new friends and chat over a
sneaky Thursday drink.

\*\*Who is it for?\*\*  
Everyone from the trans community is welcome. This is an opportunity to
be yourself, whatever you identify as. We are inclusive and happy to
welcome you.

\*\*How does it work?\*\*  
All you have to do is RSVP and then we will message you on the day with
the event location. Then, all you have to do is show up.

We will make sure that you meet some new people and get a chance to get
to know your fellow trans buddies. This event is very friendly and will
welcome you and make sure you feel comfortable and happy.  
It is free to attend, just buy yourself a drink at the bar.

closes at 16.00 on the day of the event.

events.name: Release Fundraiser: The Hub\'s Revenge
events.description:
Release is the national centre of expertise on drugs and drugs law
providing free and confidential specialist advice to the public and
professionals. Release also campaigns for changes to UK drug policy to
bring about a fairer and more compassionate legal framework to manage
drug use in our society. The UK is currently one of the deadliest
countries in Europe for people who use drugs. This situation is only
setto get worse: the spread of synthetic opioids and their contimaintion
of multiple drug supplies means is a serious concern. Given government
inaction and willingness to let people die, we need to take action and
fight against the forces preventing change around us to truly bring
change. We need spaces to keep people safe, alive, and informed. Release
opened the Harm Reduction Hub in East London this year: it is a
community drop-in centre which provides low threshold harm reduction
advice and signposting for any visitor, with the goal of benefitting
people who are traditionally underserved due to stigma – such as people
who rough sleep, use drugs, or sell sex. Through the Hub, anyone is able
to get drug test strips, drug testing kits, legal advice (similar to a
helpline), signposted to relevant services, as well as a warm drink and
a friendly face. As it is mostly funded by donations, Release is
fundraising to keep the Hub stocked, staffed, and loaded. All funds
raised will revert directly back to protecting and informing our
community on how they can keep safe and look out for each other. £7
minimum donation from 9:30pm Door Policy Dalston Superstore is a queer

events.name: Hatred Is a Bitter Fruit - Residency Writing Workshops
events.description: [ TICKETS ][1] A series of hosted writing workshops on offer every Tuesday from July 16 until August 20, between 7 to 9pm The theme of the workshops is centred around the title - *Hatred is a Bitter Fruit* - we will be exploring the many intersections and layers of hatred, hate crimes, shame and abuse, and how we respond to those lived or imagined experiences and feelings.  The workshops are open to all LGBTQIA+ communities especially those of colour. Creative writing is a form of self-expression, and within a supportive and safe environment has the potential to begin a process of healing, and is an opportunity to be heard through your choice of words on a page. Playful, experimental and at times surprising what will emerge from deep within. Your host will be Jack - a Poet-Curator and Psycho-Spiritual Dharma and Shamanic performance artist. A Zen Body Worker and Carrier of Indigenous Earth Knowledge.  They received a Spread The Word Commission Award in Autumn 2023. Recent readings include Lewisham Literature Festival, Autistic Shuffle, Devereux and with Poem Brut at Rich Mix and a Hundred Years Gallery. They received an Arts Council Project Award in 2024, to co-facilitate a series of free poetry workshops for LGBTQIA+ communities and to produce a \'free\' intersectional poetry anthology hatred is a bitter fruit that will be published in Jan/Feb 2025.  All who attend the workshops may choose to enter up to four poems for publication, and will be responding to the prompt or theme: hatred is a bitter fruit details of the call will be shared during the poetry writing workshops. All first time writers are welcome, we want poetry to be accessible to all.  There will also be co-hosts who will facilitate the workshops, the last three weeks will be an open forum for everyone to share poems that they have written or choose and there will space to write too if that is your preference.   The co-host will be Venus - a martial artist, writer and performer from Harlesden. A sex worker for many years, her work is a reflection of her experiences with unconventional notions of power, strength, sensuality, subversion and the concept of embodiment as knowledge. She is a recent graduate with a BA in Politics, Philosophy and History, and is founder of Sex and Rage, a sex worker led organisation resisting stigma and shame through sex education. For the last three weeks the co-host will be our own Lyall Hakaraia, these three final classes will be both creative and reflective of the outcomes of the workshops. The workshops are FREE but have a limited number of tickets (10 people per workshop). All attendees will be eligible for travel expenses, there will be a flat reimbursement of £10 per workshop. Pen and papers will be provided or bring your choice of pen to write with. These workshops are supported by Arts Council England. events.name: Brighton Trans Pride - Celebrate with us
events.description:
\*\*Trans Pride Brighton - Celebrate with us\*\*

Join us at Trans Pride Brighton. This was a fantastic event last year
with tens of thousands of people and we are delighted to return this
year. This is Trans Pride Brighton\'s 10 year celebration. It\'s a
really well organised event and you\'ll have an amazing time.

We are partnering with Rainbow Stores, a member\'s LGBTQAI+ business,
where you can get all of your trans party apparel there. \*\*(See below
for the discount code).\*\*

\*\*We have the regular meetup where we will do the march and then will
relax in the park after, enjoying the entertainment and then off to the
after pride official party. See below for more.\*\*

\*\*The Details:\*\*  
\*\*11.00\*\* We will be meeting at \*\*Brighton Train Station.\*\*  
\*\*11.30\*\* We will go down to Jubilee Square, to \*\*listen to the
speeches\*\* outside The Brighton Jubilee Library.

\*\*12.00: The march begins\*\* and we will join in, walking to
Brunswick Square. (This is really fun).

\*\*13.00 - 18.00\*\* There will be a speaker stage in Jubilee Square
during the afternoon, performances and community stalls at Brighton
Domes Corn Exchange from 1 until 6pm. There is a family picnic area in
Dorset Gardens with acoustic and spoken word performances, and finally a
bar in New Steine Gardens with a dance tent.

\*\*19.00 - 03.00\*\*: The after party venue is at the Corn Exchange on
the Saturday evening in central Brighton, 7pm until late and organised
by Traumfrau Brighton. This is the official after party trans
celebration - \*\*THIS IS A TICKETED EVENT AND YOU NEED TO BUY YOUR
TICKETS IN ADVANCE.\*\* The link is Tickets:
\[[https://brightondome.org/whats-on/Vgn-trans-pride-brighton-2024-afterparty/\](https://brightondome.org/whats-on/Vgn-trans-pride-brighton-2024-afterparty/][1])

\*\*As always I’ll email out the full details the day before to anyone
who has RSVP’d the day before.\*\*

\*\*Getting there:\*\*  
As we are meeting in Brighton train station, please make your own
arrangements to get there. Brighton has an excellent service from
London. It takes 90 minutes roughly from London to get there and trains
are quite regular. A direct train from Victoria takes just under 1 hour.
(\*\*Please Note:\*\* You cannot tap on with your card so please
remember to book a ticket).

\*\*About the March\*\*  
There is a vibrant trans community in Brighton and Trans Pride Brighton
started in 2013 and has grown year on year since then. Over 30,000
people attended in 2023. Let\'s help make this the best year ever.

To honour the long legacy of transgender, non-binary, gender
non-conforming and intersex people who came before us, build a placard,
wear the flag or flowers, paint your face, get involved and have fun
while you are building awareness of trans people and the trans
community.

\*\*See more at
\[[https://transpridebrighton.org/\](https://transpridebrighton.org/][2])\*\*\[
\]([https://transpridebrighton.org/][3])

\*\*Who is this for:\*\*  
This is for anyone who is trans, questioning or a supporter of trans
people.

\*\*Wanna celebrate in Pride in Style?\*\*  
We are delighted to give you a special Trans Pride offer from one of our
member\'s Trans business \[Transgender Clothes and Accessories
(therainbowstores.com)\]([https://www.therainbowstores.com/collections/transgender][4]).
Suzix has put together a special trans pack for all your pride
celebrations. Please use the code \*\*TRANSPRIDE24 to get a 20%
discount.\*\*

\*\*Please note:\*\* We do not make any money from any partner offers.
We just love to support the people who support us!

events.description:
[ TICKETS ][1] ### **One More Time: 1996**

Been watching the Top Of The Pops re-runs and want (ooh aah) just a
little bit more?!

Its 1996 and boybands ruled (even if Take That would split up). Eternal
were the only girlband in sight… until five spicey girls zig-a-zig-ah\'d
their way into history and changed the face of pop forever!

We\'ll be celebrating the year the Spice Girls entered our lives, Gina G
flew the flag for the UK in Eurovision, everyone and their gran danced
the Macarena and Louise got Naked (yet still managed to show less flesh
than Peter Andre in the waterfall). Expect A list pop from the likes of
East 17, Gabrielle, Mariah Carey and Cher, dance music from JX, Livin\'
Joy and Robert Miles, the Britpop boom from Dodgy, Ash and Sleeper and
the smooth tones of Mark Morrison, Fugees, Lighthouse Family and George
Michael. Oh and did we mention the year of Celine\'s many epic ballads
?!

Expect loads of forgotten gems you\'re unlikely to hear anywhere else
(from 1996\'s B listers such as Alisha\'s Attic to Gloria Estefan and
Pet Shop Boys to Mary Kiani). Our Bargain Bin first hour of 1996’s pop
flops (from E\'voke to Maxwell and Let Loose) kicks off from 9pm.



[1]: https://www.outsavvy.com/event/20879/one-more-time-1996

events.name: Thursday Social Drinks In Soho
events.description:
Join me and your fellow trans lovelies for a relaxed meetup which takes
place on the second \*\*Thursday of the month in the Soho, central
London area.\*\*

This place has a great buzz. It\'s a sneaky way to start the weekend
early. Come and join us :)

\*\*RSVP NOW\*\*

We have a private area upstairs in the venue, which is plenty of space
for us all to chat, hear each other and relax.

Thursday is the new start of the weekend. Let\'s use this opportunity to
make some new friends and chat about whatever pleases you.  
This event will suit you if you are new to attending the meetup or are
one of our wonderful regulars. It is a popular evening with lots of
different people popping in. There is no need to be nervous. We are all
very friendly and welcoming. You\'ll feel right at home. :)

\*\*What is this meetup?\*\*  
This is a relaxed, friendly and inclusive meetup for the trans people of
London. This is an opportunity to make new friends and chat over a
sneaky Thursday drink.

\*\*Who is it for?\*\*  
Everyone from the trans community is welcome. This is an opportunity to
be yourself, whatever you identify as. We are inclusive and happy to
welcome you.

\*\*How does it work?\*\*  
All you have to do is RSVP and then we will message you on the day with
the event location. Then, all you have to do is show up.

We will make sure that you meet some new people and get a chance to get
to know your fellow trans buddies. This event is very friendly and will
welcome you and make sure you feel comfortable and happy.  
It is free to attend, just buy yourself a drink at the bar.

\*\*Please Note:\*\* RSVP is a must as the location (based around Soho)
will be sent by email on the day to those who have RSVP\'d only. RSVP
closes at 16.00 on the day of the event.

\*\*RSVP NOW\*\*

events.description:
[ TICKETS ][1] ### **Steamed Jams **

Music Policy / Nostalgia pop and throwback dance anthems

Dress Code / Your Simpsons Icon ( yellow body paint unnecessary ) 

### **A Night Out In Springfield **

A silly, camp, Simpsons-themed party? At this time of year? At this time
of day? In this part of Dalston? Localised entirely within VFD?

Eeeh-Ye-e-e-es!

If you’re looking for a dopamine hit of nostalgia, grab your ticket
for *Steamed Jams* - a costumed club night dedicated to our four
fingered, future predicting, Flanderific friends… The Simpsons.

[MisterrCha][2] is our resident Disco Stu for the night, delivering
throwback dance anthems and feel-good tunes from 1990 to now. You might
even hear some familiar voices from our neighbourinos in the mix too.
Are you couch gagging yet?

You will be rubbing shoulders with all of the Springfield socialites, so
we invite you to dress the part of your favourite Simpsons icon. Minus
any yellow body paint.

Are you stupid sexy Flanders? What will you reveal under that mangled
Chanel dress? Or will you expose the true identity of El Homo?

Filled with absurdity and surprises, *Steamed Hams* will be
unforgettably dumbening. So don that blue beehive. Suck that pacifier.
And join us for a Flamin’ Moe’s at a one-of-a-kind night with the whole
Party Posse.

So what are you waiting for? Buy that ticket and let your brain release
some more endorphins.

Smell ya later!

events.name: Thursday Social Drinks In Soho
events.description:
Join me and your fellow trans lovelies for a relaxed meetup which takes
place on the second \*\*Thursday of the month in the Soho, central
London area.\*\*

This place has a great buzz. It\'s a sneaky way to start the weekend
early. Come and join us :)

\*\*RSVP NOW\*\*

We have a private area upstairs in the venue, which is plenty of space
for us all to chat, hear each other and relax.

Thursday is the new start of the weekend. Let\'s use this opportunity to
make some new friends and chat about whatever pleases you.  
This event will suit you if you are new to attending the meetup or are
one of our wonderful regulars. It is a popular evening with lots of
different people popping in. There is no need to be nervous. We are all
very friendly and welcoming. You\'ll feel right at home. :)

\*\*What is this meetup?\*\*  
This is a relaxed, friendly and inclusive meetup for the trans people of
London. This is an opportunity to make new friends and chat over a
sneaky Thursday drink.

\*\*Who is it for?\*\*  
Everyone from the trans community is welcome. This is an opportunity to
be yourself, whatever you identify as. We are inclusive and happy to
welcome you.

\*\*How does it work?\*\*  
All you have to do is RSVP and then we will message you on the day with
the event location. Then, all you have to do is show up.

We will make sure that you meet some new people and get a chance to get
to know your fellow trans buddies. This event is very friendly and will
welcome you and make sure you feel comfortable and happy.  
It is free to attend, just buy yourself a drink at the bar.

\*\*Please Note:\*\* RSVP is a must as the location (based around Soho)
will be sent by email on the day to those who have RSVP\'d only. RSVP
closes at 16.00 on the day of the event.

\*\*RSVP NOW\*\*

events.name: Regent's Park Intro Laps
events.description:
A gentle, supportive and informative session for anyone who wants to ride with us in a casual, no expectations way. Suitable for any kind of roadworthy bike, we\'ll spend the first hour introducing some group riding techniques and doing a few laps of the inner circle of Regent\'s Park. Afterward we all head to the cafe for a chat and get to know each other a bit better.   
  
Open to all women, trans, and non-binary people of any ability and riding experience, no membership required. Sign up via our [RiderHQ events page][1].  
  
This is held monthly on the second Saturday of the month. It is facilitated by Velociposse members who volunteer their time to lead this ride. Occasionally we may have to cancel due to bad weather or volunteer availability so please check before attending!

events.name: Femmme Fraiche
events.description:
A SEPTEMBER BENDER! Autumn is on it’s way, and we’re throwing our last
summer bender in September, come and sweat it out with us on 14th
September at the mothership Dalston Superstore. In the basement, our
headliner needs no introduction, a Dalston Superstore staple, a regular
neon-haired glow around London town and the absolute kween of
tweak-yer-nipples Hi-NRG bangers, very excited to have Angel D’Lite in
the Fèmmme Fraîche building. On opening duties we have another Dalston
Superstore regular, the multi-genre, multi-disciplied DJ and dancer
HENDERSON and of course completing the trio, sandwiched between the two,
our beloved resident Michelle Manetti. Expect hands-in-the-air Euphoria
all night long. Up top in the bar two of our fave regular guest DJ’s
return, Thempress and Areola Grande Latte and on ?2 ? closing we have
our fave duo of Fraîchness, Fèmmme Fraîche residents Linzi Symons and
Darren Skene with all your trash-tastic faves. For gogo duties, we have
our all time-fave, the icon and superstar Danni Spooner joined by
another Femmme Fraiche regular, the Hi-Octane legendary Sabrina Jade.
Expect, ass-shakin’ sexy, stupendous bar-top antics. (for low salary
income please contact us for discounted entry) With a small selection of
£5 early bird tickets and a limited number of General Admission tickets
for sale online – these allow you Q-jump and are valid for entry until
11pm only. Once these have sold out entry will be general admission
tickets available on the door, on the night. *We operate a zero
tolerance policy* Our event is FLINTA focused and aimed as a space for
queer wxmn, Trans, NB, and they will be given priority. Allies and
friends are welcome, providing they respect the space. £8 from 9 / £10

events.name: 56T trans & non-binary sexual health & wellbeing service
events.description:
56T has become a booked appointment service instead of walk-in. Appointments can be booked here: [https://www.dean.st/trans-non-binary/][1]. This service is for:  
·         Hormone injections (with proof of ID and prescription)

·         Hormone level monitoring and liver function testing

·         PrEP – Pre-Exposure Prophylaxis

·         PEP – Post-Exposure Prophylaxis

·         Confidential sexual health screening and Hepatitis B & HPV
vaccinations

·         Cervical smear tests for anyone over 25 with a cervix – not
done as walk in, but pre-booked into Tuesday AM clinic

·         Sexual assault support

·         Domestic abuse support and IDVA – Independent Domestic
Violence Advocate

·         Health advisor support and signposting into other services for
issues around housing, counselling etc.



[1]: https://www.dean.st/trans-non-binary/

events.name: Queer Family Cabaret Workshop Afternoon
events.description:
[ TICKETS ][1] Queer Family Cabaret

Welcome to a relaxed and fun afternoon for families of all ages and
abilities, to learn and explore performance skills, located at the VFD
Outsiders Gallery 64 Stoke Newington Rd. The workshop will be led by
Arkem and Sally (see their details below).

The workshop will open at 1.30 and will run between 2 and 4.30 with time
for feedback

(aim to arrive with at least 15 minutes to settle in).

The workshop begins with warm up games and an easy-to-follow process
will then help you to create a character in the moment and to find a
costume. Further games enable you to share your character and game in an
impromptu co-created cabaret in front of the appreciative and supportive
audience of your fellow participants. In cabaret the audience and
performers are equally important and so there is no pressure to perform.
This workshop will end in a celebration of each other.  
With this workshop we hope that you will have laughed and created
together as a family in a new and fun way. The workshop is held by
experienced and caring performers and will be accessible, inclusive and
responsive. Please do not hesitate to get on touch if you have any
queries.

 This workshop has been well received by families. We would like this
work to develop in a responsive way from the feedback from families and
so this will be a low-fee offering with time at the end for feedback.

The ground floor is a fully accessible space with a bathroom designed by
wheel chair users.



[1]: https://www.outsavvy.com/event/21889/queer-family-cabaret-afternoon-workshop

events.name: One More Time 2003
events.description:
[ TICKETS ][1] One More Time returns to 2003! Reality TV acts were all over the charts
from Popstars\' Girls Aloud, Liberty X, Cheeky Girls and err One True
Voice to Pop Idol\'s Will Young, Gareth Gates, Darius, Sarah Whatmore,
Zoe Birkett and Rosie Ribbons and Fame Academy\'s David Sneddon, Sinead
Quinn, Lemar, Adele Parks and Ainslie Henderson… not to mention Pop Idol
2\'s winner waiting in the wings.

It was also a big year for Dannii Minogue, Kylie, Jamelia, Christina,
Mis-Teeq and the Sugababes, not to mention Beyonce, Emma Bunton, Delta
Goodrem and Lisa Scott-Lee. We said goodbye to S Club (7), hello to
newly re-branded S Club 8, Busted took us to the Year 3000 and t.A.T.u.
raised eyebrows.

We’ll be playing the A list popstars from 2003 along with B listers like
Kym Marsh, Big Brovaz and a whole host of Clubland names along with
loads of other pop and dance hits from 2003. Expect loads of forgotten
gems you\'re unlikely to hear anywhere else (from D-Side to Abs and
Stacie Orrico). Our Bargain Bin first hour of 2003’s pop flops (from
Maria Willson to Nodesha and Alice Martineau) kicks the night off from
9pm.

£10 advance, £12 on the door



[1]: https://www.outsavvy.com/event/22060/one-more-time-2003

events.name: PERMISSION 2 REMISSION
events.description:
A NIGHT OUT ON E Superstore’s own E is fundraising to support their
mother through unemployment and an extreme lack of government support
whilst battling cancer. “My beautiful mother, Tania, was diagnosed with
cancer in December last year and has been out of work since then, coming
up on 10 months now. Up until this month, she has sustained herself on
holiday pay that she accrued over 10+ years at her minimum wage job.

She has been informed by her oncologist that she will be out of work
until February 2025 – though her accrued holiday pay ends this
September, leaving her with no income. She was also hit with an
unforeseen $200 (£100) increase in rent last May, which could not have
come at a worse time.

With no savings or assets to fall back on, my mother requested early
access to her superannuation, though this has still not been anywhere
near enough to cover her cost of living and will leave her with even
less to fall back on in ongoing years. Her expenses amount to roughly
$3000 (£1,500) a month for rent, bills, groceries and medical related
costs. I have set the fundraising goal to $20,000 (£10,000) to support
her through her time out of work. It would be a dream to come anywhere
close to that.” PERMISSION 2 REMISSION will be a certified heater:
Stacked lineup, both floors, good cause. +++ a raffle with megaaaa
prizes to be won! Come through & have a boogie for a good cause x £7
MINIMUM DONATION FROM 9pm DONATE TO E’S FUNDRAISER HERE

events.description:
Run by and at Herne Hill Velodrome in South East London. You must have completed a track induction before attending any track sessions: see [hernehillvelodrome.com][1] for details.  
  
A supportive and challenging environment in which riders of all abilities can develop their track craft through a mixture of skills, drills and workshops. £10 including bike hire.  
  
If you have completed a track training accreditation, you can join the intermediate session. Once you have done several skills sessions and feel confident that you understand the different techniques on the track you can do a training accreditation, and then join the intermediate session, which combines faster exercises, intervals to improve fitness, and introduces racing techniques.   
  
Please note that these sessions are not run by Velociposse. We recommend them because: track cycling is great for general bike handling skills (you\'re on a fixed gear bike), fitness (no stopping for traffic lights!) and confidence.

events.name: Thursday Social Drinks In Soho
events.description:
Join me and your fellow trans lovelies for a relaxed meetup which takes
place on the second \*\*Thursday of the month in the Soho, central
London area.\*\*

This place has a great buzz. It\'s a sneaky way to start the weekend
early. Come and join us :)

\*\*RSVP NOW\*\*

We have a private area upstairs in the venue, which is plenty of space
for us all to chat, hear each other and relax.

Thursday is the new start of the weekend. Let\'s use this opportunity to
make some new friends and chat about whatever pleases you.  
This event will suit you if you are new to attending the meetup or are
one of our wonderful regulars. It is a popular evening with lots of
different people popping in. There is no need to be nervous. We are all
very friendly and welcoming. You\'ll feel right at home. :)

\*\*What is this meetup?\*\*  
This is a relaxed, friendly and inclusive meetup for the trans people of
London. This is an opportunity to make new friends and chat over a
sneaky Thursday drink.

\*\*Who is it for?\*\*  
Everyone from the trans community is welcome. This is an opportunity to
be yourself, whatever you identify as. We are inclusive and happy to
welcome you.

\*\*How does it work?\*\*  
All you have to do is RSVP and then we will message you on the day with
the event location. Then, all you have to do is show up.

We will make sure that you meet some new people and get a chance to get
to know your fellow trans buddies. This event is very friendly and will
welcome you and make sure you feel comfortable and happy.  
It is free to attend, just buy yourself a drink at the bar.

\*\*Please Note:\*\* RSVP is a must as the location (based around Soho)
will be sent by email on the day to those who have RSVP\'d only. RSVP
closes at 16.00 on the day of the event.

\*\*RSVP NOW\*\*

events.name: One More DAYtime: 1998
events.description:
[ TICKETS ][1] One More Time goes daytime! Re-live your youth and enjoy the hits,
forgotten gems and flops from 1998! And get home at a reasonable hour!! 

It was the year pure pop really hit the big time with B\*Witched and
Billie making their chart debuts, Steps, Five and Aqua hitting the big
time and Cher making THAT comeback.

It was also the year Celine‘s heart went on, Des’ree had some toast,
Cleopatra came \'atcha, the Spice Girls Stop-ped as a five piece (and
said GET WELL SOON/ Goodbye to Geri) and The Honeyz and The Corrs hit
big. We were also Horny having Sex On The Beach whilst wondering what
she would look like with a chimney on her. 70\'s covers were all over
and epic ballads ruled the charts. Imaani and Dana International tussled
it out for Eurovision success whilst Brandy and Monica fought it out
over a boy.

We’ll be playing the A list popstars from 1998 along with B listers like
Lutricia McNeal, Alda and Garbage along with loads of other pop and
dance hits from 1998. Expect loads of forgotten gems you\'re unlikely to
hear anywhere else (from Ultra and Lucid to Solid HarmoniE.). Our
Bargain Bin first hour of 1998’s pop flops (from Kerri-Ann to E-Male and
Christian Fry) kicks things off for the first hour.

Come along on 19th October - the Music Sounds Better With YOU!



[1]: https://www.outsavvy.com/event/22172/one-more-daytime-1998

events.name: 10 YEARS OF SNS: SORRY STILL GOING - TIL 4AM!
events.description:
CELEBRATING 10 YEARS OF SORRY NOT SORRY  “A treasure trove of feral pop
we never knew we needed,  SNS truly is a saviour and sanctuary,  here’s
to 10 more”  – Daily Mail “SorryNotSorry is the reason I vote Tory” –
Geri Halliwell in Tudor drag “London’s Premiere Inn” – FHM Dalston
superstore’s dirty little secret,  its twisted Sunday sister with
terrible taste in pop floaters,  celebrates its 10th anniversary with
two floors and a sexy Saturday slot – Sorry Still Going (but not, of
course, lols) Longest running night at Superstore we hear you cry?  Yes
truth, but calm down hun,  have you ever even been?  Bellyflopping onto
the circuit(gay) in 2014,  SorryNotSorry has devolved over the last
decade,  a Sunday night tonic which deliciously misreads a room.
Upstairs, our carefully curated selection of DJ’s will be bringing
SorryNotSorry’s trademark sound of pop turds, treasures, and pleasures.
Meanwhile downstairs, we’ve enlisted some of our fave DJ’s to put their
own spin on the laser pit a la SorryNotSorry. With Dalston’s homegrown
cheeky girls, Dorothy Perkins and Jane Norman, slippin’ and sliding’ all
over the bar, and a coveted LIVE performance from Sharon LeGrande that
Fergie once described as “mesmerising and nonsensical”, you’ll be wetter
than Xtina getting dirteh on the d-floor! Expect lots of squeals and
shrieks from the likes of Victoria Beckham,  Lisa Scott Lee and Las
Ketchup – pop turkeys from the crypt reanimated in the most fabulous and
unhinged way.   That cork wedge & velour Juicy tracksuit combo wont
spill tequila down itself bab.  Wanna feel blessed and distressed? C U
THERE xoxooxoxoxox £8 from 10 / £10 from 11

events.name: HHV Women's Training
events.description:
Run by and at Herne Hill Velodrome in South East London. You must have completed a track induction before attending any track sessions: see [hernehillvelodrome.com][1] for details.  
  
A supportive and challenging environment in which riders of all abilities can develop their track craft through a mixture of skills, drills and workshops. £10 including bike hire.  
  
If you have completed a track training accreditation, you can join the intermediate session. Once you have done several skills sessions and feel confident that you understand the different techniques on the track you can do a training accreditation, and then join the intermediate session, which combines faster exercises, intervals to improve fitness, and introduces racing techniques.   
  
Please note that these sessions are not run by Velociposse. We recommend them because: track cycling is great for general bike handling skills (you\'re on a fixed gear bike), fitness (no stopping for traffic lights!) and confidence.  

[1]: http://hernehillvelodrome.com

events.name: t'ART Exhibition: Queer Time - Private View
events.description:
[ TICKETS ][1] We are really excited to be bringing together queer and trans artists
and makers for a new exhibition at The Outsiders Gallery, responding to
the theme of \'queer time\'. 

Time is different for us. The markers of a life have not always been
accessible to queer people: marriage, children, their children and so
on. And then there’s coming out, again and again. Transitioning,
changing our bodies, changing our pronouns. Many of us explore as our
true selves late. 

We have gathered work from both emerging and established queer and trans
artists, working across a variety of disciplines from painting to
photography, film to sculpture. And we can’t wait to share it with you.

We’d love for you to join us to celebrate the exhibition’s opening at
our Private View on 2nd November. Tickets are available for a suggested
donation of £3 and all proceeds go towards the exhibition’s costs, or
you can purchase one of our most recent publications to pick up at the
event! Drinks will be available to purchase at the bar.



[1]: https://www.outsavvy.com/event/22879/tart-exhibition-queer-time-private-view

events.name: Thursday Social Drinks In Soho
events.description:
Join me and your fellow trans lovelies for a relaxed meetup which takes
place on the second \*\*Thursday of the month in the Soho, central
London area.\*\*

This place has a great buzz. It\'s a sneaky way to start the weekend
early. Come and join us :)

\*\*RSVP NOW\*\*

We have a private area upstairs in the venue, which is plenty of space
for us all to chat, hear each other and relax.

Thursday is the new start of the weekend. Let\'s use this opportunity to
make some new friends and chat about whatever pleases you.  
This event will suit you if you are new to attending the meetup or are
one of our wonderful regulars. It is a popular evening with lots of
different people popping in. There is no need to be nervous. We are all
very friendly and welcoming. You\'ll feel right at home. :)

\*\*What is this meetup?\*\*  
This is a relaxed, friendly and inclusive meetup for the trans people of
London. This is an opportunity to make new friends and chat over a
sneaky Thursday drink.

\*\*Who is it for?\*\*  
Everyone from the trans community is welcome. This is an opportunity to
be yourself, whatever you identify as. We are inclusive and happy to
welcome you.

\*\*How does it work?\*\*  
All you have to do is RSVP and then we will message you on the day with
the event location. Then, all you have to do is show up.

We will make sure that you meet some new people and get a chance to get
to know your fellow trans buddies. This event is very friendly and will
welcome you and make sure you feel comfortable and happy.  
It is free to attend, just buy yourself a drink at the bar.

\*\*Please Note:\*\* RSVP is a must as the location (based around Soho)
will be sent by email on the day to those who have RSVP\'d only. RSVP
closes at 16.00 on the day of the event.

\*\*RSVP NOW\*\*

events.description:

non-binary people at Omnibus Theatre in Clapham, London on Friday 15
November 2024, 7-8:30pm.We will split the speed dating into two
groups:20s-40s40s+The intention is to give you the choice of which group

minutes to spark up a good conversation. You’ll get a digital form at

of benefit. :)Date: Friday 15 November 2024Time: 7-8:30pmLocation:

0QWAccessibility: The venue and toilets are step-free and wheelchair

events.description:
Run by and at Herne Hill Velodrome in South East London. You must have completed a track induction before attending any track sessions: see [hernehillvelodrome.com][1] for details.  
  
A supportive and challenging environment in which riders of all abilities can develop their track craft through a mixture of skills, drills and workshops. £10 including bike hire.  
  
If you have completed a track training accreditation, you can join the intermediate session. Once you have done several skills sessions and feel confident that you understand the different techniques on the track you can do a training accreditation, and then join the intermediate session, which combines faster exercises, intervals to improve fitness, and introduces racing techniques.   
  
Please note that these sessions are not run by Velociposse. We recommend them because: track cycling is great for general bike handling skills (you\'re on a fixed gear bike), fitness (no stopping for traffic lights!) and confidence.

events.name: No Drama! - Reading Trans representation on screen and other film making crimes
events.description:
[ FREE TICKETS ][1] On Wednesday Nov 20 VFDalston will be hosting a shadey look at the
history of Trans representation on the big screen, how Hollywood and
indie film makers have portrayed trans characters, and our fabulous
panel of industry experts will discuss the good and the (often) bad
examples.

The talk will be proceeded by a 45 minute montage of clips from films
highlighting the ground breakingly great, the jaw droppingly awful and
the downright offensive.

We will task our panel with creating a Manifesto of demands for future
film makers to consult.

Then we will open up for questions and statements from the audience.

As well as in person tickets, we will be hosting the evening online, so
you can sign up for an IRL ticket or a streaming link.

The venue will be The Outsiders Gallery at VFDalston, No64 Stoke
Newington Road.

The space is fully accessible with a small ramp at the front door from
the high street, and a newly installed wheelchair user designed
bathroom.

Our panelists include Jaye Hudson (she/her) (TGirls on Film), Rue
Lumbroso (she/her) Transmissions, Tara Brown (they/them) Fringe! Queer
Film & Arts Festival, Molly Miles (they/them) Catagory H horror club
and Trans Buffet, plus more TBC

Tickets are FREE, but we do ask if you cannot attend please let us know
so we can reallocate your ticket.

Supported by Hackney365, as part of Hackney Pride 365 - Transgender
Awareness Week



[1]: https://www.outsavvy.com/event/22844/no-drama-reading-trans-representation-on-screen-and-other-film-making-crimes
events.summary: No Drama! - Reading Trans representation on screen and other film making crimes

events.description:

A supportive and challenging environment in which riders of all abilities can develop their track craft through a mixture of skills, drills and workshops. £10 including bike hire.  
  
If you have completed a track training accreditation, you can join the intermediate session. Please note that these sessions are not run by Velociposse. We recommend them because: track cycling is great for general bike handling skills (you\'re on a fixed gear bike), fitness (no stopping for traffic lights!) and confidence.

events.name: Queer House Party
events.description:
7/12/24London’s hottest queer party is back, featuring DJs, live shows,
drag performances, strippers, dancers, voguing takeovers, and vendors.
The lineup will be dropping soon. VENUE:We host our parties at No. 90
Hackney Wick—a large warehouse with multiple rooms. This means we’ll
have a stacked lineup across two spaces, offering areas to watch shows,
dance, and relax. No. 90 Hackney Wick is easily accessible via the
Overground. ACCESS:No. 90 is a wheelchair-accessible venue. Our
in-person and online events will have British Sign Language (BSL)
available during the shows, though no hearing induction loop is
installed. We also have a welfare team, with one member trained in BSL.
Free tickets are available for carers and personal assistants (PAs). If
you have any questions, please email us at queerhouseparty@gmail.com.
TICKETS AND GUEST LIST:Queer House Party is for everyone, but trans
people to the front. We’ve worked hard to keep ticket prices affordable.
Tickets are on a sliding scale from £7.50–£20. If cost is still a
barrier for you, send us a message and we’ll add you to our free
list.Low-income Tickets: For those receiving Universal Credit or
equivalent, working-class students, and people earning minimum wage.
These are limited, so please be mindful before purchasing.Standard
Tickets: For those on a salary, students, comfortable freelancers, or
those who are “skint atm” but have some savings.Solidarity Tickets: For
those financially stable enough that rent and bills aren’t a daily
struggle (this could be you—take a moment to reflect. ).Carer and
Support Worker Tickets: Free with no questions asked.Guest List and
Discount Codes: If none of these options work for you, our guest list is
reserved for people who can’t afford ticket prices. Email us at
qhptickets@gmail.com, and we’ll sort it out—no need to disclose any
personal details about your situation.VIPs: If you consider yourself a
VIP, this probably isn’t the party for you.Queer House Party is all
about celebrating everybody—no apologies, no filters. This is your space
to be loud and 100% you. Mutual respect is a must, and consent isn’t up
for debate. We’re here to build each other up and tear down anything
that gets in the way of feeling safe and free. Zero Tolerance Policy on
Harassment and DiscriminationAt Queer House Party, we are committed to
creating a safe and inclusive space for everyone. We have a
zero-tolerance policy towards any form of harassment, discrimination, or
abusive behaviour based on race, gender, sexual orientation, disability,
religion, or any other personal characteristic. Anyone engaging in such
behaviour will be asked to leave immediately. Consent is vital and
non-negotiable. Security &amp; Welfare TeamWe have a dedicated
welfare team from Safe Only on hand all night. If you experience or
witness any of the behaviours detailed above, please report to the
welfare team or the venue's security as soon as possible.Substance
PolicyWe encourage responsible alcoholic drinking and plenty of
hydration. Our bar serves a range of alcoholic and non-alcoholic options
to suit all preferences. If you think you've had too much, reach out to
our welfare team, who will be able to help. Aggressive or unsafe
behaviour towards anyone will not be tolerated.Entry PolicyYou must
bring your ID for entry. We also reserve the right to refuse entry to
anyone whose actions or attitudes conflict with these values, ensuring
that our event remains a welcoming environment for all.COVID:To help
keep the party safe, we ask that everyone take a test before attending.
If you can’t get a test beforehand, we’ll have some available at the
door.

Please note that these sessions are not run by Velociposse. We recommend them because: track cycling is great for general bike handling skills (you\'re on a fixed gear bike), fitness (no stopping for traffic lights!) and confidence.

events.name: Thursday Social Drinks In Soho
events.description:
Join me and your fellow trans lovelies for a relaxed meetup which takes
place on the second \*\*Thursday of the month in the Soho, central
London area.\*\*

This place has a great buzz. It\'s a sneaky way to start the weekend
early. Come and join us :)

\*\*RSVP NOW\*\*

We have a private area upstairs in the venue, which is plenty of space
for us all to chat, hear each other and relax.

Thursday is the new start of the weekend. Let\'s use this opportunity to
make some new friends and chat about whatever pleases you.  
This event will suit you if you are new to attending the meetup or are
one of our wonderful regulars. It is a popular evening with lots of
different people popping in. There is no need to be nervous. We are all
very friendly and welcoming. You\'ll feel right at home. :)

\*\*What is this meetup?\*\*  
This is a relaxed, friendly and inclusive meetup for the trans people of
London. This is an opportunity to make new friends and chat over a
sneaky Thursday drink.

\*\*Who is it for?\*\*  
Everyone from the trans community is welcome. This is an opportunity to
be yourself, whatever you identify as. We are inclusive and happy to
welcome you.

\*\*How does it work?\*\*  
All you have to do is RSVP and then we will message you on the day with
the event location. Then, all you have to do is show up.

We will make sure that you meet some new people and get a chance to get
to know your fellow trans buddies. This event is very friendly and will
welcome you and make sure you feel comfortable and happy.  
It is free to attend, just buy yourself a drink at the bar.

\*\*Please Note:\*\* RSVP is a must as the location (based around Soho)
will be sent by email on the day to those who have RSVP\'d only. RSVP
closes at 16.00 on the day of the event.

\*\*RSVP NOW\*\*

events.name: Drag Tales - Gipsy Hill Taproom
events.description:
Due to the lovely support from the families of Gipsy Hill, we\'re BACK
at the Gipsy Hill Taproom for a Halloweeny and a Christmas themed Drag
Tales!

The fabulous Tania LeCoq will read stories, and we\'ve made it Pay What
You Can donation to the artist to make it as accessible as possible.

Bring your kids down for a fun outing to see the stories in the books
brought to life! Please help us to make this a massive success by either
bringing your family down for a fun night or by helping us spread the
word. If these two go well as well, we can keep it going in 2025!

Let us know you\'re coming here: draggedaroundlondon.com/gipsyhilldrag

events.name: Queer Youth Art Collective
events.description:
****QUEER YOUTH ART COLLECTIVE (QYAC)** **12pm – 4pm – ONLINE GROUP 2pm
– 3.30pm****

**[Queer Youth Art Collective][1] (QYAC) has run workshops at The
Outside Project for LGBTQ young people 18-26 since August 2019. The
project delivers newly commissioned workshops by LGBTQ artists and youth
forums for attendees to discuss their practice and socialise weekly on
Sundays.**

**Our primary aims are to challenge isolation, provide free and engaging
arts workshops and build skills and infrastructure for a resilient,
peer-led LGBTQ arts and education culture in London and throughout the
UK.**

**We currently run 2 groups: ONLINE on ZOOM & OFFLINE at The Outside
Project LGBTIQ+ Centre. **

****How to access: Email queeryouthartcollective@gmail.com**. **Travel
refund available. ****



[1]: https://qyac.org.uk/

events.name: HHV Women's Training
events.description:
Run by and at Herne Hill Velodrome in South East London. You must have completed a track induction before attending any track sessions: see [hernehillvelodrome.com][1] for details.  
  
A supportive and challenging environment in which riders of all abilities can develop their track craft through a mixture of skills, drills and workshops. £10 including bike hire.  
  
If you have completed a track training accreditation, you can join the intermediate session. Once you have done several skills sessions and feel confident that you understand the different techniques on the track you can do a training accreditation, and then join the intermediate session, which combines faster exercises, intervals to improve fitness, and introduces racing techniques.   
  
Please note that these sessions are not run by Velociposse. We recommend them because: track cycling is great for general bike handling skills (you\'re on a fixed gear bike), fitness (no stopping for traffic lights!) and confidence.  

[1]: http://hernehillvelodrome.com

events.name: 56T trans & non-binary sexual health & wellbeing service
events.description:
56T has become a booked appointment service instead of walk-in. Appointments can be booked here: [https://www.dean.st/trans-non-binary/][1]. This service is for:  
·         Hormone injections (with proof of ID and prescription)

·         Hormone level monitoring and liver function testing

·         PrEP – Pre-Exposure Prophylaxis

·         PEP – Post-Exposure Prophylaxis

·         Confidential sexual health screening and Hepatitis B & HPV
vaccinations

·         Cervical smear tests for anyone over 25 with a cervix – not
done as walk in, but pre-booked into Tuesday AM clinic

·         Sexual assault support

·         Domestic abuse support and IDVA – Independent Domestic
Violence Advocate

·         Health advisor support and signposting into other services for
issues around housing, counselling etc.



[1]: https://www.dean.st/trans-non-binary/
events.summary: 56T trans & non-binary sexual health & wellbeing service

events.name: STAR Lounge
events.description:
STAR Lounge is a weekly space for those with experience of domestic
abuse and sexual violence. Come to spend time with us and talk with
people if you need, have some food and hot drinks, relax in the quiet
room or on our sofas. Once a month we have haircuts from Open Barbers
and massage therapy.

We’re proud to have created a safe, accessible and welcoming space for
survivor support at our LGBTIQ+ Centre all day on Thursdays.

DM us on Instagram or email Star.Lounge@lgbtiqoutside.org if you want to
join the STAR Lounge social group on Thursdays 10.30-4pm.

hire. Beginner friendly.

Please note this session is not run by Velociposse and may be subject to

knowledgeable coach, Nadine. You\'ll progress quickly, and have a hell
of a lot of fun.

events.name: Richmond Park Intro Laps
events.description:
A gentle, supportive and informative session for anyone who wants to ride with us in a casual, no expectations way. Suitable for any kind of roadworthy bike, we\'ll spend the first hour introducing some group riding techniques and doing a lap or two of Richmond Park. Afterward we all head to the cafe for a chat and get to know each other a bit better.   
  
Open to all women, trans, and non-binary people of any ability and riding experience, no membership required. Sign up via our [RiderHQ events page][1].  
  
This is held monthly on the fourth Saturday of the month. It is facilitated by Velociposse members who volunteer their time to lead this ride. Occasionally we may have to cancel due to bad weather or volunteer availability so please check before attending! 

[1]: https://www.riderhq.com/o/p/7odu8dgn/f/velociposse/enter

events.name: Gravel Club
events.description:
Ad-hoc ride arranged by members taking in the trails of Epping Forest. Decent confidence needed: come to our slow skills sessions first if you\'re not sure.  
  
Usually: 7pm meeting in East London. Gravel or offroad bikes. 2-3 hour ride: good quality front light essential as this ride ends after nightfall and the trails are unlit. May pause over winter in bad/cold weather, but will run as often as we can!  
  
Arranged via Discord.  
  
Contact us if you\'re interested and not already in the club! [https://forms.gle/2Fk9VvqHg8HbEehMA][1]

events.description:

issues around housing, counselling etc.

events.name: STAR Lounge
events.description:
STAR Lounge is a weekly space for those with experience of domestic
abuse and sexual violence. Come to spend time with us and talk with
people if you need, have some food and hot drinks, relax in the quiet
room or on our sofas. Once a month we have haircuts from Open Barbers
and massage therapy.

survivor support at our LGBTIQ+ Centre all day on Thursdays.

DM us on Instagram or email Star.Lounge@lgbtiqoutside.org if you want to
join the STAR Lounge social group on Thursdays 10.30-4pm.

events.name: Regent's Park Intro Laps
events.description:
A gentle, supportive and informative session for anyone who wants to ride with us in a casual, no expectations way. Suitable for any kind of roadworthy bike, we\'ll spend the first hour introducing some group riding techniques and doing a few laps of the inner circle of Regent\'s Park. Afterward we all head to the cafe for a chat and get to know each other a bit better.   
  
Open to all women, trans, and non-binary people of any ability and riding experience, no membership required. Sign up via our [RiderHQ events page][1].  
  
This is held monthly on the second Saturday of the month. It is facilitated by Velociposse members who volunteer their time to lead this ride. Occasionally we may have to cancel due to bad weather or volunteer availability so please check before attending! 

[1]: https://www.riderhq.com/o/p/7odu8dgn/f/velociposse/enter

events.name: Queer Youth Art Collective
events.description:
****QUEER YOUTH ART COLLECTIVE (QYAC)** **12pm – 4pm – ONLINE GROUP 2pm
– 3.30pm****

**[Queer Youth Art Collective][1] (QYAC) has run workshops at The
Outside Project for LGBTQ young people 18-26 since August 2019. The
project delivers newly commissioned workshops by LGBTQ artists and youth
forums for attendees to discuss their practice and socialise weekly on
Sundays.**

**Our primary aims are to challenge isolation, provide free and engaging
arts workshops and build skills and infrastructure for a resilient,
peer-led LGBTQ arts and education culture in London and throughout the
UK.**

**We currently run 2 groups: ONLINE on ZOOM & OFFLINE at The Outside
Project LGBTIQ+ Centre. **

****How to access: Email queeryouthartcollective@gmail.com**. **Travel
refund available. ****



[1]: https://qyac.org.uk/

events.name: HHV Women's Training
events.description:
Run by and at Herne Hill Velodrome in South East London. You must have completed a track induction before attending any track sessions: see [hernehillvelodrome.com][1] for details.  
  
A supportive and challenging environment in which riders of all abilities can develop their track craft through a mixture of skills, drills and workshops. £10 including bike hire.  
  
If you have completed a track training accreditation, you can join the intermediate session. Once you have done several skills sessions and feel confident that you understand the different techniques on the track you can do a training accreditation, and then join the intermediate session, which combines faster exercises, intervals to improve fitness, and introduces racing techniques.   
  
Please note that these sessions are not run by Velociposse. We recommend them because: track cycling is great for general bike handling skills (you\'re on a fixed gear bike), fitness (no stopping for traffic lights!) and confidence.  

[1]: http://hernehillvelodrome.com

events.name: HHV Women's Training
events.description:
Run by and at Herne Hill Velodrome in South East London. You must have completed a track induction before attending any track sessions: see [hernehillvelodrome.com][1] for details.  
  
A supportive and challenging environment in which riders of all abilities can develop their track craft through a mixture of skills, drills and workshops. £10 including bike hire.  
  
If you have completed a track training accreditation, you can join the intermediate session. Once you have done several skills sessions and feel confident that you understand the different techniques on the track you can do a training accreditation, and then join the intermediate session, which combines faster exercises, intervals to improve fitness, and introduces racing techniques.   
  
Please note that these sessions are not run by Velociposse. We recommend them because: track cycling is great for general bike handling skills (you\'re on a fixed gear bike), fitness (no stopping for traffic lights!) and confidence.  

[1]: http://hernehillvelodrome.com

events.name: Regent's Park Intro Laps
events.description:
A gentle, supportive and informative session for anyone who wants to ride with us in a casual, no expectations way. Suitable for any kind of roadworthy bike, we\'ll spend the first hour introducing some group riding techniques and doing a few laps of the inner circle of Regent\'s Park. Afterward we all head to the cafe for a chat and get to know each other a bit better.   
  
Open to all women, trans, and non-binary people of any ability and riding experience, no membership required. Sign up via our [RiderHQ events page][1].  
  
This is held monthly on the second Saturday of the month. It is facilitated by Velociposse members who volunteer their time to lead this ride. Occasionally we may have to cancel due to bad weather or volunteer availability so please check before attending!

events.name: 56T trans & non-binary sexual health & wellbeing service
events.description:
56T has become a booked appointment service instead of walk-in. Appointments can be booked here: [https://www.dean.st/trans-non-binary/][1]. This service is for:  
·         Hormone injections (with proof of ID and prescription)

·         Hormone level monitoring and liver function testing

·         PrEP – Pre-Exposure Prophylaxis

·         PEP – Post-Exposure Prophylaxis

·         Confidential sexual health screening and Hepatitis B & HPV
vaccinations

·         Cervical smear tests for anyone over 25 with a cervix – not
done as walk in, but pre-booked into Tuesday AM clinic

·         Sexual assault support

·         Domestic abuse support and IDVA – Independent Domestic
Violence Advocate

·         Health advisor support and signposting into other services for
issues around housing, counselling etc.



[1]: https://www.dean.st/trans-non-binary/

events.name: 56T trans & non-binary sexual health & wellbeing service
events.description:
56T has become a booked appointment service instead of walk-in. Appointments can be booked here: [https://www.dean.st/trans-non-binary/][1]. This service is for:  
·         Hormone injections (with proof of ID and prescription)

·         Hormone level monitoring and liver function testing

·         PrEP – Pre-Exposure Prophylaxis

·         PEP – Post-Exposure Prophylaxis

·         Confidential sexual health screening and Hepatitis B & HPV
vaccinations

·         Cervical smear tests for anyone over 25 with a cervix – not
done as walk in, but pre-booked into Tuesday AM clinic

·         Sexual assault support

·         Domestic abuse support and IDVA – Independent Domestic
Violence Advocate

·         Health advisor support and signposting into other services for
issues around housing, counselling etc.



[1]: https://www.dean.st/trans-non-binary/

events.description:

events.name: STAR Lounge
events.description:
STAR Lounge is a weekly space for those with experience of domestic
abuse and sexual violence. Come to spend time with us and talk with
people if you need, have some food and hot drinks, relax in the quiet
room or on our sofas. Once a month we have haircuts from Open Barbers
and massage therapy.

We’re proud to have created a safe, accessible and welcoming space for
survivor support at our LGBTIQ+ Centre all day on Thursdays.

DM us on Instagram or email Star.Lounge@lgbtiqoutside.org if you want to
join the STAR Lounge social group on Thursdays 10.30-4pm.

– 3.30pm****

Outside Project for LGBTQ young people 18-26 since August 2019. The
project delivers newly commissioned workshops by LGBTQ artists and youth
forums for attendees to discuss their practice and socialise weekly on
Sundays.**

peer-led LGBTQ arts and education culture in London and throughout the

****How to access: Email queeryouthartcollective@gmail.com**. **Travel
refund available. ****

events.name: HHV Women's Training
events.description:
Run by and at Herne Hill Velodrome in South East London. You must have completed a track induction before attending any track sessions: see [hernehillvelodrome.com][1] for details.  
  
A supportive and challenging environment in which riders of all abilities can develop their track craft through a mixture of skills, drills and workshops. £10 including bike hire.  
  
If you have completed a track training accreditation, you can join the intermediate session. Once you have done several skills sessions and feel confident that you understand the different techniques on the track you can do a training accreditation, and then join the intermediate session, which combines faster exercises, intervals to improve fitness, and introduces racing techniques.   
  
Please note that these sessions are not run by Velociposse. We recommend them because: track cycling is great for general bike handling skills (you\'re on a fixed gear bike), fitness (no stopping for traffic lights!) and confidence.  

[1]: http://hernehillvelodrome.com

events.name: Richmond Park Intro Laps
events.description:
A gentle, supportive and informative session for anyone who wants to ride with us in a casual, no expectations way. Suitable for any kind of roadworthy bike, we\'ll spend the first hour introducing some group riding techniques and doing a lap or two of Richmond Park. Afterward we all head to the cafe for a chat and get to know each other a bit better.   
  
Open to all women, trans, and non-binary people of any ability and riding experience, no membership required. Sign up via our [RiderHQ events page][1].  
  
This is held monthly on the fourth Saturday of the month. It is facilitated by Velociposse members who volunteer their time to lead this ride. Occasionally we may have to cancel due to bad weather or volunteer availability so please check before attending! 

[1]: https://www.riderhq.com/o/p/7odu8dgn/f/velociposse/enter

events.name: HHV Women's Training

**[Queer Youth Art Collective][1] (QYAC) has run workshops at The

project delivers newly commissioned workshops by LGBTQ artists and youth
forums for attendees to discuss their practice and socialise weekly on
Sundays.**

**Our primary aims are to challenge isolation, provide free and engaging
arts workshops and build skills and infrastructure for a resilient,
peer-led LGBTQ arts and education culture in London and throughout the
UK.**

Project LGBTIQ+ Centre. **

refund available. ****

events.name: HHV Women's Training
events.description:
Run by and at Herne Hill Velodrome in South East London. You must have completed a track induction before attending any track sessions: see [hernehillvelodrome.com][1] for details.  
  
A supportive and challenging environment in which riders of all abilities can develop their track craft through a mixture of skills, drills and workshops. £10 including bike hire.  
  
If you have completed a track training accreditation, you can join the intermediate session. Once you have done several skills sessions and feel confident that you understand the different techniques on the track you can do a training accreditation, and then join the intermediate session, which combines faster exercises, intervals to improve fitness, and introduces racing techniques.   
  
Please note that these sessions are not run by Velociposse. We recommend them because: track cycling is great for general bike handling skills (you\'re on a fixed gear bike), fitness (no stopping for traffic lights!) and confidence.  

[1]: http://hernehillvelodrome.com

events.name: 56T trans & non-binary sexual health & wellbeing service
events.description:
56T has become a booked appointment service instead of walk-in. Appointments can be booked here: [https://www.dean.st/trans-non-binary/][1]. This service is for:  
·         Hormone injections (with proof of ID and prescription)

·         Hormone level monitoring and liver function testing

·         PrEP – Pre-Exposure Prophylaxis

·         PEP – Post-Exposure Prophylaxis

·         Confidential sexual health screening and Hepatitis B & HPV
vaccinations

·         Cervical smear tests for anyone over 25 with a cervix – not
done as walk in, but pre-booked into Tuesday AM clinic

·         Sexual assault support

·         Domestic abuse support and IDVA – Independent Domestic
Violence Advocate

·         Health advisor support and signposting into other services for
issues around housing, counselling etc.



[1]: https://www.dean.st/trans-non-binary/

events.description:

abuse and sexual violence. Come to spend time with us and talk with
people if you need, have some food and hot drinks, relax in the quiet
room or on our sofas. Once a month we have haircuts from Open Barbers
and massage therapy.

survivor support at our LGBTIQ+ Centre all day on Thursdays.

DM us on Instagram or email Star.Lounge@lgbtiqoutside.org if you want to
join the STAR Lounge social group on Thursdays 10.30-4pm.

events.name: Regent's Park Intro Laps
events.description:
A gentle, supportive and informative session for anyone who wants to ride with us in a casual, no expectations way. Suitable for any kind of roadworthy bike, we\'ll spend the first hour introducing some group riding techniques and doing a few laps of the inner circle of Regent\'s Park. Afterward we all head to the cafe for a chat and get to know each other a bit better.   
  
Open to all women, trans, and non-binary people of any ability and riding experience, no membership required. Sign up via our [RiderHQ events page][1].  
  
This is held monthly on the second Saturday of the month. It is facilitated by Velociposse members who volunteer their time to lead this ride. Occasionally we may have to cancel due to bad weather or volunteer availability so please check before attending! 

[1]: https://www.riderhq.com/o/p/7odu8dgn/f/velociposse/enter

events.name: Richmond Park Intro Laps
events.description:
A gentle, supportive and informative session for anyone who wants to ride with us in a casual, no expectations way. Suitable for any kind of roadworthy bike, we\'ll spend the first hour introducing some group riding techniques and doing a lap or two of Richmond Park. Afterward we all head to the cafe for a chat and get to know each other a bit better.   
  
Open to all women, trans, and non-binary people of any ability and riding experience, no membership required. Sign up via our [RiderHQ events page][1].  
  
This is held monthly on the fourth Saturday of the month. It is facilitated by Velociposse members who volunteer their time to lead this ride. Occasionally we may have to cancel due to bad weather or volunteer availability so please check before attending! 

[1]: https://www.riderhq.com/o/p/7odu8dgn/f/velociposse/enter

Check with the venue for details! May be subject to change.

Womens BMX session at Lee Valley Velopark. £10 including bike and helmet
hire. Beginner friendly.

Please note this session is not run by Velociposse and may be subject to
change: you should get in touch with the venue if you have any
questions. Pre-booking required.

Why we recommend this session: it\'s where a lot of us had our first
taste of BMX, and now some of us are hooked. It\'s super beginner
friendly, a lovely community of welcoming women, and run by a superb and
knowledgeable coach, Nadine. You\'ll progress quickly, and have a hell
of a lot of fun.

events.name: HHV Women's Training
events.description:
Run by and at Herne Hill Velodrome in South East London. You must have completed a track induction before attending any track sessions: see [hernehillvelodrome.com][1] for details.  
  
A supportive and challenging environment in which riders of all abilities can develop their track craft through a mixture of skills, drills and workshops. £10 including bike hire.  
  
If you have completed a track training accreditation, you can join the intermediate session. Once you have done several skills sessions and feel confident that you understand the different techniques on the track you can do a training accreditation, and then join the intermediate session, which combines faster exercises, intervals to improve fitness, and introduces racing techniques.   
  
Please note that these sessions are not run by Velociposse. We recommend them because: track cycling is great for general bike handling skills (you\'re on a fixed gear bike), fitness (no stopping for traffic lights!) and confidence.  

[1]: http://hernehillvelodrome.com

events.name: HHV Women's Track Induction/Taster session
events.description:
An introduction to track cycling for riders of all abilities, where
you\'ll learn the basic skills that enable you to access a variety of
training sessions at Herne Hill Velodrome.

Monthly on the first Sunday of the month. Must be pre- booked: £20
including bike hire. hernehillvelodrome.com

Please note this session is not run by Velociposse.
